2.22.s:
vasiṣṭa uvāca
evaṃ dharmāṅgado rājyaṃ cakāra vasudhātale /
piturnaniyogādrājendra pālayan harivāsaram //
2.22.d:
वसिष्ट उवाच
एवं धर्माङ्गदो राज्यं चकार वसुधातले ।
पितुर्ननियोगाद्राजेन्द्र पालयन् हरिवासरम् ॥
2.22.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus Dharmāṅgada ruled the realm upon the surface of the earth / at his father's direction, O king of kings, observing the day of Hari.

2.22.s:
na babhūva janaḥ kaścidyo na dharme vyavasthitaḥ /
nāsukhī nāprajaḥ kaścinna vā phuṣṭhī mahīpate //
2.22.d:
न बभूव जनः कश्चिद्यो न धर्मे व्यवस्थितः ।
नासुखी नाप्रजः कश्चिन्न वा फुष्ठी महीपते ॥
2.22.m: There was no person who was not established in righteousness; / no one was unhappy, childless, or afflicted with leprosy, O protector of the earth.

2.22.s:
hṛṣṭapuṣṭa jane tasmin kṣmā caiva nidhidāyinī /
ghaṭadogdhrīṣu nṛpate tṛptavatsāsu dhenuṣu //
2.22.d:
हृष्टपुष्ट जने तस्मिन् क्ष्मा चैव निधिदायिनी ।
घटदोग्ध्रीषु नृपते तृप्तवत्सासु धेनुषु ॥
2.22.m: While the people were joyful and thriving, the earth yielded treasures, / and cows, whose calves were satisfied, yielded potfuls of milk, O king.

2.22.s:
puṭake kuṭake kṣaudraṃ droṇamātraṃ drume drume /
prahṛṣṭāyāṃ tu medinyāṃ sarvadhānyasamudbhavaḥ //
2.22.d:
पुटके कुटके क्षौद्रं द्रोणमात्रं द्रुमे द्रुमे ।
प्रहृष्टायां तु मेदिन्यां सर्वधान्यसमुद्भवः ॥
2.22.m: On every tree there were small hollows yielding a droṇa of honey; / and while the earth was delighted, all varieties of grain sprang forth.

2.22.s:
kṛtasya sparddhini yuge tretānte dvāpare yuge /
vyatīte jaladāpāye nirmale cāṃbare gṛhe //
2.22.d:
कृतस्य स्पर्द्धिनि युगे त्रेतान्ते द्वापरे युगे ।
व्यतीते जलदापाये निर्मले चांबरे गृहे ॥
2.22.m: In the Dvāpara age, at the close of the Tretā age, rivaling the Kṛta age, / when the cessation of the rains had passed, and the sky was clear and clouds were gone,

2.22.s:
sugandhiśālipakvāḍhye kuṃbhodbhavavilokite /
madhyapravāhayuktāsu nimnagāsu samantataḥ //
2.22.d:
सुगन्धिशालिपक्वाढ्ये कुंभोद्भवविलोकिते ।
मध्यप्रवाहयुक्तासु निम्नगासु समन्ततः ॥
2.22.m: when the earth was rich with ripe, fragrant rice, watched over by Agastya, / and rivers flowed with a moderate current everywhere,

2.22.s:
tīrotthaiḥ kāśapuṣpaiśca śuklakeśairivāṅganā /
candrāṃśudhavale loke nātitīvre divākare //
2.22.d:
तीरोत्थैः काशपुष्पैश्च शुक्लकेशैरिवाङ्गना ।
चन्द्रांशुधवले लोके नातितीव्रे दिवाकरे ॥
2.22.m: when the banks bloomed with kāśa flowers like women with white hair, / when the world was white with moonbeams and the sun was not overly hot,

2.22.s:
tasminmanuṣyabahulairjalasnānavicitritaiḥ /
yatrotsukaiḥ prayātaistu bhūmipālaiḥ samantataḥ //
2.22.d:
तस्मिन्मनुष्यबहुलैर्जलस्नानविचित्रितैः ।
यत्रोत्सुकैः प्रयातैस्तु भूमिपालैः समन्ततः ॥
2.22.m: at that time, crowded with men variegated by water-baths, / and kings had set out everywhere, eager for festivities,

2.22.s:
prabodhasamaye viṣṇorāśvinānte jagadguroḥ /
mohinī ramayāmāsa tatkāle hṛcchayārditā //
2.22.d:
प्रबोधसमये विष्णोराश्विनान्ते जगद्गुरोः ।
मोहिनी रमयामास तत्काले हृच्छयार्दिता ॥
2.22.m: at the time of the awakening of Viṣṇu, the teacher of the world, at the end of the month of Āśvina, / Mohinī, afflicted by love at that time, delighted

2.22.s:
rājānaṃ vividhaiḥ saukhyaiḥ sarvabhāvena suṃdarī /
vaneṣu giriśṛṅgeṣu nadīnāṃ saṃgameṣu ca //
2.22.d:
राजानं विविधैः सौख्यैः सर्वभावेन सुंदरी ।
वनेषु गिरिशृङ्गेषु नदीनां संगमेषु च ॥
2.22.m: the king with diverse pleasures wholeheartedly, being a beautiful woman, / in the forests, on mountain peaks, and at the confluences of rivers,

2.22.s:
padminī kusumāḍhyeṣu saraḥsu vividheṣu ca /
malaye mandare vindhye mahendre vibudhālaye //
2.22.d:
पद्मिनी कुसुमाढ्येषु सरःसु विविधेषु च ।
मलये मन्दरे विन्ध्ये महेन्द्रे विबुधालये ॥
2.22.m: at various lakes abundant with lotus blossoms, / on Malaya, Mandara, Vindhya, Mahendra, in the abode of the gods,

2.22.s:
sahye prāleyasaṃjñe ca digaṃbaragirau śubhe /
anyeṣu caiva rājānaṃ svargasthānādikeṣu ca //
2.22.d:
सह्ये प्रालेयसंज्ञे च दिगंबरगिरौ शुभे ।
अन्येषु चैव राजानं स्वर्गस्थानादिकेषु च ॥
2.22.m: on the auspicious Sahya, the mountain called snowy [Himālaya], and Digambara, / and in other heavenly realms and the like, she delighted

2.22.s:
rameyāyāsa rājendra divyarūpā dine dine /
rājāpi mohinīṃ prāpya sarvaṃ kṛtyaṃ parityajan //
2.22.d:
रमेयायास राजेन्द्र दिव्यरूपा दिने दिने ।
राजापि मोहिनीं प्राप्य सर्वं कृत्यं परित्यजन् ॥
2.22.m: the king, O king of kings, appearing in divine form day after day. / The king too, having gained Mohinī, abandoned all other duties;

2.22.s:
tyaktaṃ na vāsaraṃ viṣṇorjanmamṛtyunikṛntanam /
vrataṃ nopekṣate tattu atimugdho 'pi pārthivaḥ //
2.22.d:
त्यक्तं न वासरं विष्णोर्जन्ममृत्युनिकृन्तनम् ।
व्रतं नोपेक्षते तत्तु अतिमुग्धो ऽपि पार्थिवः ॥
2.22.m: yet he did not abandon the day of Viṣṇu, which cuts off birth and death. / Even though utterly infatuated, that king did not neglect the vow.

2.22.s:
krīḍāṃ tyajati bhūpālo daśamyādidinatraye /
evaṃ prakīḍatastasya pūrṇe saṃvatsare gate //
2.22.d:
क्रीडां त्यजति भूपालो दशम्यादिदिनत्रये ।
एवं प्रकीडतस्तस्य पूर्णे संवत्सरे गते ॥
2.22.m: The ruler of the earth abandoned dalliance during the three days beginning with the tenth. / As he was sporting thus, when a full year had elapsed,

2.22.s:
kāle kālavidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ saṃprāptaḥ kārtikaḥ śubhaḥ /
nidrāchedakaro viṣṇoḥ sa māsaḥ puṇyadāyakaḥ //
2.22.d:
काले कालविदां श्रेष्ठः संप्राप्तः कार्तिकः शुभः ।
निद्राछेदकरो विष्णोः स मासः पुण्यदायकः ॥
2.22.m: the auspicious month of Kārtika arrived in due time, O best of those who know time— / that month which ends the sleep of Viṣṇu and bestows merit,

2.22.s:
yasminkṛtaṃ hi sukṛtaṃ vaiṣṇavairmanujairnṛpa /
akṣayaṃ hi bhavetsarvaṃ viṣṇulokapradāyakam //
2.22.d:
यस्मिन्कृतं हि सुकृतं वैष्णवैर्मनुजैर्नृप ।
अक्षयं हि भवेत्सर्वं विष्णुलोकप्रदायकम् ॥
2.22.m: in which good deeds performed by Vaiṣṇava men, O king, / all become imperishable, granting the world of Viṣṇu.

2.22.s:
na kārtikasamo māso na kūtena samaṃ yugam /
na dharmastu dayā tulyo na jyotiścakṣuṣā samam //
2.22.d:
न कार्तिकसमो मासो न कूतेन समं युगम् ।
न धर्मस्तु दया तुल्यो न ज्योतिश्चक्षुषा समम् ॥
2.22.m: There is no month equal to Kārtika; there is no yuga equal to the Kṛta; / there is no duty equal to compassion; there is no light equal to the eye.

2.22.s:
na vedena samaṃ śāstraṃ na tīrthaṃ gaṅgayā samam /
na bhūmyā sadṛśaṃ dānaṃ na sukhaṃ bhāryayā samam //
2.22.d:
न वेदेन समं शास्त्रं न तीर्थं गङ्गया समम् ।
न भूम्या सदृशं दानं न सुखं भार्यया समम् ॥
2.22.m: There is no scripture equal to the Veda; there is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā; / there is no gift equal to land; there is no happiness equal to a wife.

2.22.s:
na kṛṣyā tu samaṃ vittaṃ na lābhaḥ surabhīsamaḥ /
na tapo 'naśanādanyanna damena samaṃ śivam //
2.22.d:
न कृष्या तु समं वित्तं न लाभः सुरभीसमः ।
न तपो ऽनशनादन्यन्न दमेन समं शिवम् ॥
2.22.m: There is no wealth equal to agriculture; there is no gain equal to a wish-granting cow; / there is no austerity other than fasting; there is no auspicious good equal to self-control.

2.22.s:
tṛptirna rasanātulyā na samo 'nyo dvijena ca /
na dharmeṇa samaṃ mitraṃ na satyena samaṃ yaśaḥ //
2.22.d:
तृप्तिर्न रसनातुल्या न समो ऽन्यो द्विजेन च ।
न धर्मेण समं मित्रं न सत्येन समं यशः ॥
2.22.m: There is no satisfaction equal to taste; there is none equal to a twice-born; / there is no friend equal to righteousness; there is no fame equal to truth.

2.22.s:
nārogyasamamaiśvaryaṃ na devaḥ keśavātparaḥ /
na kārtikasamaṃ loke pāvanaṃ kavayo viduḥ //
2.22.d:
नारोग्यसममैश्वर्यं न देवः केशवात्परः ।
न कार्तिकसमं लोके पावनं कवयो विदुः ॥
2.22.m: There is no sovereignty equal to health; there is no deity higher than Keśava; / poets know no purifier in the world equal to Kārtika.

2.22.s:
kārtikaḥ pravaro māso viṣṇoścāpi priyaḥ sadā /
avrato hi kṣipedyastu māsaṃ dāmodarapriyam //
2.22.d:
कार्तिकः प्रवरो मासो विष्णोश्चापि प्रियः सदा ।
अव्रतो हि क्षिपेद्यस्तु मासं दामोदरप्रियम् ॥
2.22.m: Kārtika is the foremost month and ever dear to Viṣṇu. / Whosoever passes the month dear to Dāmodara without vows

2.22.s: tiryagyonimavāpnoti sarvadharmabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
2.22.d: तिर्यग्योनिमवाप्नोति सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥
2.22.m: attains an animal birth, excluded from all duties.

2.22.s:
māndhātovāca
saṃprāpya kārtike māse rājā rukmāṅgado mune /
mohinīṃ mohasaṃyuktāṃ kathaṃ sa bubhuje vada //
2.22.d:
मान्धातोवाच
संप्राप्य कार्तिके मासे राजा रुक्माङ्गदो मुने ।
मोहिनीं मोहसंयुक्तां कथं स बुभुजे वद ॥
2.22.m: Māndhātṛ said: / “When the month of Kārtika arrived, O sage, how did King Rukmāṅgada / enjoy Mohinī, who was filled with infatuation? Tell me.

2.22.s:
viṣṇubhaktaḥ śrutiparaḥ pravaraḥ sa mahīkṣitām /
tasminpuṇyatame māse kiṃ cakāra nṛpottamaḥ //
2.22.d:
विष्णुभक्तः श्रुतिपरः प्रवरः स महीक्षिताम् ।
तस्मिन्पुण्यतमे मासे किं चकार नृपोत्तमः ॥
2.22.m: He was devoted to Viṣṇu, intent upon the scriptures, the foremost of monarchs. / What did that best of kings do in that most holy month?”

2.22.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
saṃprāptaṃ kārtikaṃ dṛṣṭvā prabodhakaraṇaṃ hareḥ /
atipramugdho rājendro mohinīṃ vākyamabravīt //
2.22.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
संप्राप्तं कार्तिकं दृष्ट्वा प्रबोधकरणं हरेः ।
अतिप्रमुग्धो राजेन्द्रो मोहिनीं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
2.22.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Seeing the arrival of Kārtika, which brings about the awakening of Hari, the king of kings, deeply infatuated, spoke words to Mohinī:

2.22.s:
rataṃ devi tvayā sārddhaṃ mayā saṃvatsarānbahūn /
tavāpamānabhītena noktaṃ kiñcidapi kvacit //
2.22.d:
रतं देवि त्वया सार्द्धं मया संवत्सरान्बहून् ।
तवापमानभीतेन नोक्तं किञ्चिदपि क्वचित् ॥
2.22.m: "O lady, I have sported with you for many years; / fearing your displeasure, I have never said anything anywhere.

2.22.s:
sāṃprataṃ vaktukāmo 'haṃ tannibodha śubhānane /
tvayyāsaktasya me devi bahavaḥ kārtikā gatāḥ //
2.22.d:
सांप्रतं वक्तुकामो ऽहं तन्निबोध शुभानने ।
त्वय्यासक्तस्य मे देवि बहवः कार्तिका गताः ॥
2.22.m: Now I desire to speak; understand that, O fair-faced woman! / For me who am attached to you, O lady, many Kārtikas have passed.

2.22.s:
na vratī kārtike jāto muktvaikaṃ harivāsaram /
so 'haṃ kārtikamicchāmi vrate na paryyupāsitum //
2.22.d:
न व्रती कार्तिके जातो मुक्त्वैकं हरिवासरम् ।
सो ऽहं कार्तिकमिच्छामि व्रते न पर्य्युपासितुम् ॥
2.22.m: I did not undertake a vow in Kārtika, except for the one day of Hari. / Therefore, I desire to attend to Kārtika with a vow.

2.22.s:
avratena gato yeṣāṃ kārtiko martyadharmiṇām /
iṣṭāpūrtau vṛthā teṣāṃ dharmo druhiṇasaṃbhave //
2.22.d:
अव्रतेन गतो येषां कार्तिको मर्त्यधर्मिणाम् ।
इष्टापूर्तौ वृथा तेषां धर्मो द्रुहिणसंभवे ॥
2.22.m: For those mortal beings for whom Kārtika has passed without a vow, / their religious duty in sacrificial and charitable works is useless, O daughter of Brahmā.

2.22.s:
māṃsāśino 'pi bhūpālā atyarthaṃ mṛgayāratāḥ /
te bhāṃsaṃ kārtike tyaktvā gatā viṣṇvālayaṃ śubhe //
2.22.d:
मांसाशिनो ऽपि भूपाला अत्यर्थं मृगयारताः ।
ते भांसं कार्तिके त्यक्त्वा गता विष्ण्वालयं शुभे ॥
2.22.m: Even kings who ate meat and were excessively devoted to hunting, / having given up meat in Kārtika, went to Viṣṇu's abode, O fair one.

2.22.s:
pravṛttānāṃ hi bhakṣyāṇāṃ kārtike niyame kṛte /
avaśyaṃ viṣṇurūpatvaṃ prāpyate sādhakena hi //
2.22.d:
प्रवृत्तानां हि भक्ष्याणां कार्तिके नियमे कृते ।
अवश्यं विष्णुरूपत्वं प्राप्यते साधकेन हि ॥
2.22.m: Indeed, when an observance is made regarding everyday foods in Kārtika, / similarity of form with Viṣṇu is certainly attained by the practitioner.

2.22.s:
tiṣṭhantu bahuvittāni dānāni varavarṇini /
hṛdayāyāsakartṝṇi dīpadānāddivaṃ vrajet //
2.22.d:
तिष्ठन्तु बहुवित्तानि दानानि वरवर्णिनि ।
हृदयायासकर्तॄणि दीपदानाद्दिवं व्रजेत् ॥
2.22.m: Leave aside gifts of great wealth that cause exertion to the heart, O woman of excellent complexion; / through the offering of a lamp one goes to heaven.

2.22.s:
tasyāpyabhāvātsubhage paradīpaprabodhanam /
kartavyaṃ bhaktibhāvena sarvadānādhikaṃ ca tat //
2.22.d:
तस्याप्यभावात्सुभगे परदीपप्रबोधनम् ।
कर्तव्यं भक्तिभावेन सर्वदानाधिकं च तत् ॥
2.22.m: Even in the absence of that, O auspicious one, trimming another's lamp / should be performed with a spirit of devotion; and that is greater than all gifts.

2.22.s:
ekataḥ sarvadānāni dīpadānaṃ hi caikataḥ /
kārtikena samaṃ proktaṃ dīpadānātprabodhanam //
2.22.d:
एकतः सर्वदानानि दीपदानं हि चैकतः ।
कार्तिकेन समं प्रोक्तं दीपदानात्प्रबोधनम् ॥
2.22.m: All gifts are on one side, and the gift of a lamp is on the other; / keeping a lamp burning is proclaimed equal to Kārtika [observances] through the gift of a lamp.

2.22.s:
kartavyaṃ bhaktibhāvena sarvadānādhikaṃ smṛtam /
kārtikīṃ ca tithiṃ kṛtvā viṣṇornābhisaroruhe //
2.22.d:
कर्तव्यं भक्तिभावेन सर्वदानाधिकं स्मृतम् ।
कार्तिकीं च तिथिं कृत्वा विष्णोर्नाभिसरोरुहे ॥
2.22.m: It should be performed with a spirit of devotion; it is remembered as superior to all gifts. / And having observed the full-moon lunar day of Kārtika at the navel-lotus of Viṣṇu,

2.22.s:
ājanmakṛtapāpāttu mucyate nātrasaṃśayaḥ /
vratopavāsaniyamaiḥ kārtiko yasya gacchati //
2.22.d:
आजन्मकृतपापात्तु मुच्यते नात्रसंशयः ।
व्रतोपवासनियमैः कार्तिको यस्य गच्छति ॥
2.22.m: one is freed from sins committed since birth; there is no doubt in this. / For whomever Kārtika passes with vows, fasts, and observances,

2.22.s:
devo vaimāniko bhūtvā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim /
tasmānmohini mohaṃ tvaṃ parityajya mamopari //
2.22.d:
देवो वैमानिको भूत्वा स याति परमां गतिम् ।
तस्मान्मोहिनि मोहं त्वं परित्यज्य ममोपरि ॥
2.22.m: becoming a god travelling in an aerial car, he goes to the supreme state. / Therefore, O Mohinī, giving up your infatuation toward me,

2.22.s:
ājñāṃ vidhehi tatkālaṃ kariṣye kārttikavratam /
tava vakṣojapūjāyā virato nīrajekṣame //
2.22.d:
आज्ञां विधेहि तत्कालं करिष्ये कार्त्तिकव्रतम् ।
तव वक्षोजपूजाया विरतो नीरजेक्षमे ॥
2.22.m: grant your permission; at that time I will perform the vow of Kārtika. / Desisting from the worship of your breasts, O lotus-eyed woman,

2.22.s:
ahaṃ vratadharaścaiva bhaviṣye haripūjane /
mohinyuvāca
vistareṇa samākhyāhi māhātmyaṃ kārtikasya ca //
2.22.d:
अहं व्रतधरश्चैव भविष्ये हरिपूजने ।
मोहिन्युवाच
विस्तरेण समाख्याहि माहात्म्यं कार्तिकस्य च ॥
2.22.m: I shall indeed maintain the vow in the worship of Hari." / Mohinī said: / "Explain in detail the eulogy of greatness of Kārtika.

2.22.s:
sarvapuṇyākaraḥ prokto māso 'yaṃ rājasattamā /
viśeṣātkutra kathitastadādiśa mahāmate //
2.22.d:
सर्वपुण्याकरः प्रोक्तो मासो ऽयं राजसत्तमा ।
विशेषात्कुत्र कथितस्तदादिश महामते ॥
2.22.m: This month is said to be a mine of all merits, O best of kings; / tell where it is especially proclaimed, O highly intelligent one!

2.22.s: śrutvā kārttikamāhātmyaṃ kariṣye 'haṃ yathepsitam //
2.22.d: श्रुत्वा कार्त्तिकमाहात्म्यं करिष्ये ऽहं यथेप्सितम् ॥
2.22.m: Having heard the eulogy of the greatness of Kārtika, I shall act as you desire."

2.22.s:
rukmāṅgada uvāca
māhātmyamabhidhāsyāmi māsasyāsya varānane /
yena bhaktirbhavitrī te prakartuṃ haripūjanam //
2.22.d:
रुक्माङ्गद उवाच
माहात्म्यमभिधास्यामि मासस्यास्य वरानने ।
येन भक्तिर्भवित्री ते प्रकर्तुं हरिपूजनम् ॥
2.22.m: Rukmāṅgada said: / "I shall describe the eulogy of the greatness of this month, O fair-faced one, / by which devotion will arise in you to perform the worship of Hari.

2.22.s:
kārttike kṛcchrasevī yaḥ prājāpatyacaro 'pi vā /
ekāntaropavāsī vā trirātropoṣito 'pi vā //
2.22.d:
कार्त्तिके कृच्छ्रसेवी यः प्राजापत्यचरो ऽपि वा ।
एकान्तरोपवासी वा त्रिरात्रोपोषितो ऽपि वा ॥
2.22.m: Whoever performs the kṛcchra in Kārtika, or practices the prājāpatya, / or fasts on alternate days, or even fasts for three nights,

2.22.s:
yadvā daśāhaṃ pakṣaṃ vā māsaṃ vā varavarṇini /
kṣapayitvā naro yāti sa viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
2.22.d:
यद्वा दशाहं पक्षं वा मासं वा वरवर्णिनि ।
क्षपयित्वा नरो याति स विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
2.22.m: or, O woman of excellent complexion, having spent ten days, a fortnight, or a month [fasting], / that man goes to the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

2.22.s:
ekabhaktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca /
asmin narairdharā caiva prāpyate dvīpamālinī //
2.22.d:
एकभक्तेन नक्तेन तथैवायाचितेन च ।
अस्मिन् नरैर्धरा चैव प्राप्यते द्वीपमालिनी ॥
2.22.m: By eating once a day, by eating at night, and likewise by eating only unsolicited food / in this [month], the earth garlanded with continents is attained by men.

2.22.s:
viśeṣātpuṣkare tīrthe dvārāvatyāṃ ca śaukare /
māso 'yaṃ bhaktidaḥ prokto vratadānārcanādibhiḥ //
2.22.d:
विशेषात्पुष्करे तीर्थे द्वारावत्यां च शौकरे ।
मासो ऽयं भक्तिदः प्रोक्तो व्रतदानार्चनादिभिः ॥
2.22.m: Especially at the sacred ford of Puṣkara, at Dvārāvatī, and at Śaukara, / this month is declared to bestow devotion through vows, gifts, worship, and the like.

2.22.s:
tasninhari dinaṃ puṇyaṃ tathā vai bhīṣmapañcakam /
prabodhinīṃ naraḥ kṛtvā jāgareṇa samanvitām //
2.22.d:
तस्निन्हरि दिनं पुण्यं तथा वै भीष्मपञ्चकम् ।
प्रबोधिनीं नरः कृत्वा जागरेण समन्विताम् ॥
2.22.m: In that [month] the sacred day of Hari and the Bhīṣmapañcaka [occur]; / a man who observes the Prabodhinī accompanied by a vigil

2.22.s:
na māturjaṭhare tiṣṭhedapi pāpānvito naraḥ /
tasmindine varārohe maṇḍalaṃ yastu paśyati //
2.22.d:
न मातुर्जठरे तिष्ठेदपि पापान्वितो नरः ।
तस्मिन्दिने वरारोहे मण्डलं यस्तु पश्यति ॥
2.22.m: does not stay in a mother's womb, even if the man is endowed with sin. / On that day, O woman of lovely hips, whoever beholds a sacred diagram,

2.22.s:
vinā sāṃkhyena yogena sa yāti paramaṃ padam /
kārtike maṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaukareḥ sūkaraṃ śubhe //
2.22.d:
विना सांख्येन योगेन स याति परमं पदम् ।
कार्तिके मण्डलं दृष्ट्वा शौकरेः सूकरं शुभे ॥
2.22.m: even without Sāṃkhya or Yoga, goes to the supreme abode. / Having seen a sacred diagram in Kārtika, [or] the Boar of Śaukara, O fair one,

2.22.s:
dṛṣṭvā kokavarāhaṃ vā na bhūyastanayo bhavet /
trividhasyāpi pāpasya dṛṣṭvā muktirbhavennṛṇām //
2.22.d:
दृष्ट्वा कोकवराहं वा न भूयस्तनयो भवेत् ।
त्रिविधस्यापि पापस्य दृष्ट्वा मुक्तिर्भवेन्नृणाम् ॥
2.22.m: or having seen Kokāvarāha, one does not become a child [in a womb] again. / For men, liberation from even the threefold sin occurs upon seeing

2.22.s:
maṇḍalaṃ capalāpāṅgi śrīdharaṃ kubjake tathā /
kārtike varjayettailaṃ kārttike varjayenmadhu //
2.22.d:
मण्डलं चपलापाङ्गि श्रीधरं कुब्जके तथा ।
कार्तिके वर्जयेत्तैलं कार्त्तिके वर्जयेन्मधु ॥
2.22.m: the sacred diagram, O woman with tremulous eyes, [or] Śrīdhara at Kubjaka. / In Kārtika one should avoid oil; in Kārtika one should avoid honey;

2.22.s:
kārtike varjayenmāṃsaṃ kārtike varjayetstriyaḥ /
niṣpāvānkārtike devi tyañjedviṣṇutatparaḥ //
2.22.d:
कार्तिके वर्जयेन्मांसं कार्तिके वर्जयेत्स्त्रियः ।
निष्पावान्कार्तिके देवि त्यञ्जेद्विष्णुतत्परः ॥
2.22.m: in Kārtika one should avoid meat; in Kārtika one should avoid women. / In Kārtika, O lady, one devoted to Viṣṇu should abandon flat beans.

2.22.s:
saṃvatsarakṛtātpāpādbrahirbhavati tatkṣaṇāt /
prāpnoti rājakīṃ yoniṃ sakṛdbhakṣaṇasaṃbhavāt //
2.22.d:
संवत्सरकृतात्पापाद्ब्रहिर्भवति तत्क्षणात् ।
प्राप्नोति राजकीं योनिं सकृद्भक्षणसंभवात् ॥
2.22.m: From the sin committed throughout a year, he is freed at that very moment. / From eating [them] even once, one incurs rebirth as a washerman.

2.22.s:
kārtike śaukaramāṃsaṃ yastu bhuñjīta durmatiḥ /
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi raurave paripacyate //
2.22.d:
कार्तिके शौकरमांसं यस्तु भुञ्जीत दुर्मतिः ।
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि रौरवे परिपच्यते ॥
2.22.m: The evil-minded one who eats pig's meat in Kārtika / is cooked in Raurava for sixty thousand years.

2.22.s:
tanmukto jāyate pāpī viṣṭhāśī grāmyasūkaraḥ /
mātsyaṃ māṃsaṃ na bhuñjīta na kaurmaṃ nāpi hāriṇam //
2.22.d:
तन्मुक्तो जायते पापी विष्ठाशी ग्राम्यसूकरः ।
मात्स्यं मांसं न भुञ्जीत न कौर्मं नापि हारिणम् ॥
2.22.m: Released from that, the sinner is born as an excrement-eating village boar. / One should not eat the meat of fish, nor that of turtle, nor that of deer.

2.22.s:
cāṇḍālo jāyate devi kārtike māṃsabhakṣaṇāt /
kārtikaḥ sarvapāpaghnaḥ kiñcidvratadharasya hi //
2.22.d:
चाण्डालो जायते देवि कार्तिके मांसभक्षणात् ।
कार्तिकः सर्वपापघ्नः किञ्चिद्व्रतधरस्य हि ॥
2.22.m: A person is born as an outcaste, O lady, from eating meat in Kārtika. / Kārtika destroys all sins for one who keeps even a slight vow.

2.22.s:
kārtike tu kṛtādīkṣā nṛṇāṃ janmanikṛntanī /
tasmātsarvaprayatnena dīkṣāṃ kurvīta kārtike //
2.22.d:
कार्तिके तु कृतादीक्षा नृणां जन्मनिकृन्तनी ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन दीक्षां कुर्वीत कार्तिके ॥
2.22.m: Initiation undertaken in Kārtika cuts away the rebirths of men; / therefore, with all effort, one should take initiation in Kārtika.

2.22.s:
adīkṣitasya vāmoru kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ nirarthakam /
paśuyonimavāpnoti dīkṣayā rahito naraḥ //
2.22.d:
अदीक्षितस्य वामोरु कृतं सर्वं निरर्थकम् ।
पशुयोनिमवाप्नोति दीक्षया रहितो नरः ॥
2.22.m: For an uninitiated person, O fair-thighed one, whatever is done is useless; / devoid of initiation, a man enters the womb of an animal.

2.22.s:
na gṛhe kārtikaṃ kuryādviśeṣeṇa tu kārtikīm /
tīrthe hi kārtikīṃ kurvannaro yāti hareḥ padam //
2.22.d:
न गृहे कार्तिकं कुर्याद्विशेषेण तु कार्तिकीम् ।
तीर्थे हि कार्तिकीं कुर्वन्नरो याति हरेः पदम् ॥
2.22.m: One should not observe Kārtika at home, and especially not the full moon of Kārtika; / for observing the full moon of Kārtika at a sacred ford, a man goes to Hari's abode.

2.22.s:
kārtike śuklapakṣasya kagṛtvā hyekādaśīṃ naraḥ /
prātardatvā śubhānkuṃbhānprayāti harimandiram //
2.22.d:
कार्तिके शुक्लपक्षस्य कगृत्वा ह्येकादशीं नरः ।
प्रातर्दत्वा शुभान्कुंभान्प्रयाति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
2.22.m: Having observed the eleventh day of the bright fortnight in Kārtika, / and giving auspicious water-pots in the morning, a man goes to the temple of Hari.

2.22.s:
saṃvatsaravratānāṃ hi samāptiḥ kārtikaṃ smṛtā /
vivāhā yatra dṛśyante viṣṇornābhisaroruhe //
2.22.d:
संवत्सरव्रतानां हि समाप्तिः कार्तिकं स्मृता ।
विवाहा यत्र दृश्यन्ते विष्णोर्नाभिसरोरुहे ॥
2.22.m: The completion of vows lasting a year is remembered to be in Kārtika, / where marriages are seen [performed] at the navel-lotus of Viṣṇu.

2.22.s:
dināni tatra catvāri yathaikaṃ varāvarṇini /
vinottarāyaṇe kālaṃ lagnaśuddhiṃ vināpi ca //
2.22.d:
दिनानि तत्र चत्वारि यथैकं वरावर्णिनि ।
विनोत्तरायणे कालं लग्नशुद्धिं विनापि च ॥
2.22.m: The four days there are like one [day], O woman of excellent complexion; / without the period of the northern course of the sun, and even without an auspicious astrological moment,

2.22.s:
dṛśyante yatra sambandhāḥ putrapautravivarddhanāḥ /
tasmānmohini kartāsmi kārtike vratasevanam //
2.22.d:
दृश्यन्ते यत्र सम्बन्धाः पुत्रपौत्रविवर्द्धनाः ।
तस्मान्मोहिनि कर्तास्मि कार्तिके व्रतसेवनम् ॥
2.22.m: alliances are seen there that increase sons and grandsons. / Therefore, O Mohinī, I will undertake the practice of the vow in Kārtika

2.22.s:
aśeṣapāpanāśāya tava prītivivṛddhaye /
mohinyuvāca
aho māhātmyamatulaṃ kārtikasya tvayoritam //
2.22.d:
अशेषपापनाशाय तव प्रीतिविवृद्धये ।
मोहिन्युवाच
अहो माहात्म्यमतुलं कार्तिकस्य त्वयोरितम् ॥
2.22.m: for the destruction of endless sins and for the enhancement of your pleasure." / Mohinī said: / "Ah, the peerless greatness of Kārtika has been spoken by you!

2.22.s:
cāturmāsyavratānāṃ hi vidhimudyāpanaṃ vada /
pūrṇatā yena bhavatagi vratānāṃ pṛthivīpate //
2.22.d:
चातुर्मास्यव्रतानां हि विधिमुद्यापनं वद ।
पूर्णता येन भवतगि व्रतानां पृथिवीपते ॥
2.22.m: Tell the concluding rite and rule of the vows of the four months of the rainy season, / by which, O lord of the earth, the completion of the vows takes place,

2.22.s:
avaikalyaṃ bhaveccaiva vrataṃ puṇyaphalasya tu /
rājovāca
naktavratī ṣaḍrasena brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayetpriye //
2.22.d:
अवैकल्यं भवेच्चैव व्रतं पुण्यफलस्य तु ।
राजोवाच
नक्तव्रती षड्रसेन ब्राह्मणं भोजयेत्प्रिये ॥
2.22.m: and the vow of meritorious fruit will be without deficiency." / The king said: / "One observing the vow of eating at night should feed a brāhmaṇa with food of six flavors, O beloved.

2.22.s:
ayācite tvanaṅkāhaṃ sahiraṇyaṃ pradāpayet /
amāṃsāśībhavedyasttu gāṃ pradadyātsadakṣiṇām //
2.22.d:
अयाचिते त्वनङ्काहं सहिरण्यं प्रदापयेत् ।
अमांसाशीभवेद्यस्त्तु गां प्रदद्यात्सदक्षिणाम् ॥
2.22.m: In the vow of eating unsolicited food, he should give an ox along with gold; / and he who refrains from eating meat should give a cow along with a priestly gift.

2.22.s:
dhātrīsnāne naro dadyāddadhipāyasameva ca /
phalānāṃ niyame subhru phaladānaṃ samācaret //
2.22.d:
धात्रीस्नाने नरो दद्याद्दधिपायसमेव च ।
फलानां नियमे सुभ्रु फलदानं समाचरेत् ॥
2.22.m: For the bath with myrobalan, a man should give curds and milk-rice pudding; / in the restriction of fruits, O fair-browed one, he should perform the donation of fruits.

2.22.s:
tailatyāge ghṛtaṃ dadyā ddhṛtatyāge payastathā /
dhānyānāṃ niyame śālīṃstattaddhānyamathāpi vā //
2.22.d:
तैलत्यागे घृतं दद्या द्धृतत्यागे पयस्तथा ।
धान्यानां नियमे शालींस्तत्तद्धान्यमथापि वा ॥
2.22.m: In renouncing oil he should give ghee, and in renouncing ghee, milk; / in the restriction of grains, rice, or those very grains.

2.22.s:
dadyādbhūśayane śayyāṃ tūlikāgaṇḍakānvitām /
patrabhojī narodadyādbhājanaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam //
2.22.d:
दद्याद्भूशयने शय्यां तूलिकागण्डकान्विताम् ।
पत्रभोजी नरोदद्याद्भाजनं घृतसंयुतम् ॥
2.22.m: When observing sleeping on the ground, he should give a bed furnished with a mattress and pillows; / a man who eats from leaves should give a vessel filled with ghee.

2.22.s:
maune ghaṇṭāṃ tilānvāpi sahiraṇyānpradāpayet /
daṃpatyorbhojanaṃ kāryamubhayoḥ śayanānvitam //
2.22.d:
मौने घण्टां तिलान्वापि सहिरण्यान्प्रदापयेत् ।
दंपत्योर्भोजनं कार्यमुभयोः शयनान्वितम् ॥
2.22.m: In the vow of silence he should give a bell or sesame seeds with gold; / a meal should be offered to a married couple together with a bed,

2.22.s:
saṃbhogaṃ dakṣiṇopetaṃ vratasya paripūrtaye /
prātaḥ snāne hayaṃ dadyānniḥsnehe ghṛtasaktukān //
2.22.d:
संभोगं दक्षिणोपेतं व्रतस्य परिपूर्तये ।
प्रातः स्नाने हयं दद्यान्निःस्नेहे घृतसक्तुकान् ॥
2.22.m: and provisions accompanied by a priestly gift, for the complete fulfillment of the vow; / for the morning bath he should give a horse; in the avoidance of unctuous food, ghee and barley meal.

2.22.s:
nakharāṇāṃ ca keśānāṃ dhāraṇe darpaṇaṃ dadet /
upānahau pradadyāttu pādatrāṇavivarjane //
2.22.d:
नखराणां च केशानां धारणे दर्पणं ददेत् ।
उपानहौ प्रदद्यात्तु पादत्राणविवर्जने ॥
2.22.m: In keeping nails and hair [uncut], one should give a mirror; / but when foregoing footwear, one should give a pair of sandals.

2.22.s:
lavaṇasya tu saṃtyāge dātavyā surabhistathā /
āmiṣasya parityāge savatsāṃ kapilāṃ dadet //
2.22.d:
लवणस्य तु संत्यागे दातव्या सुरभिस्तथा ।
आमिषस्य परित्यागे सवत्सां कपिलां ददेत् ॥
2.22.m: When completely giving up salt, a cow should be given; / and upon renouncing meat, one should give a brown cow with its calf.

2.22.s:
nityaṃ dīpaprado yastu vrate 'bhīṣṭe surālaye /
sa kāñcanaṃ tathā tāmraṃ saghṛtaṃ dīpakaṃ priye //
2.22.d:
नित्यं दीपप्रदो यस्तु व्रते ऽभीष्टे सुरालये ।
स काञ्चनं तथा ताम्रं सघृतं दीपकं प्रिये ॥
2.22.m: One who daily offers a lamp in the temple of a deity during a cherished vow, / he, O lovely one, should give a lamp made of gold or copper along with clarified butter,

2.22.s:
pradadyādvāsasā chatraṃ vaiṣṇave vratapūrtaye /
ekāntaropavāsī tu kṣaumavastraṃ pradāpayet //
2.22.d:
प्रदद्याद्वाससा छत्रं वैष्णवे व्रतपूर्तये ।
एकान्तरोपवासी तु क्षौमवस्त्रं प्रदापयेत् ॥
2.22.m: And an umbrella with cloth, to a Vaiṣṇava, to complete the vow. / One who fasts on alternate days should give a linen garment.

2.22.s:
trirātre kāñcanopetāṃ dadyācchayyāṃ svalaṅkṛtām /
ṣaḍrarātrādyupavāseṣu śibikāṃ chatrasaṃyutām //
2.22.d:
त्रिरात्रे काञ्चनोपेतां दद्याच्छय्यां स्वलङ्कृताम् ।
षड्ररात्राद्युपवासेषु शिबिकां छत्रसंयुताम् ॥
2.22.m: For a fast of three nights, one should give a well-adorned bed furnished with gold; / for fasts of six nights and the like, a palanquin with an umbrella,

2.22.s:
savāhapuruṣaṃ pīnamanaṅvāhamathārpayet /
ajāvikaṃ tvekabhakte phalāhāre suvarṇakam //
2.22.d:
सवाहपुरुषं पीनमनङ्वाहमथार्पयेत् ।
अजाविकं त्वेकभक्ते फलाहारे सुवर्णकम् ॥
2.22.m: And then offer a stout draft-ox along with a driver. / When eating once a day, [one should give] a goat or sheep; when living on fruit, [a piece of] gold;

2.22.s:
śākāhāre phalaṃ dadyātsauvarṇaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam /
rasānāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ tyāge 'nuktasya vāpi ca //
2.22.d:
शाकाहारे फलं दद्यात्सौवर्णं घृतसंयुतम् ।
रसानां चैव सर्वेषां त्यागे ऽनुक्तस्य वापि च ॥
2.22.m: When living on vegetables, one should give a golden fruit accompanied by clarified butter. / When giving up all juices, or [when giving up] whatever has not been specified,

2.22.s:
dātavyaṃ rājataṃ pātraṃ sauvarṇa vāpi śaktitaḥ /
yathoktasyāpradāne tu yathoktākaraṇe 'pi vā //
2.22.d:
दातव्यं राजतं पात्रं सौवर्ण वापि शक्तितः ।
यथोक्तस्याप्रदाने तु यथोक्ताकरणे ऽपि वा ॥
2.22.m: A silver vessel, or a golden one according to one's capacity, should be given. / If one fails to give what has been prescribed, or fails to do what has been enjoined,

2.22.s:
vipravākyaṃ caretsubhru viṣṇusmaraṇapūrvakam /
vṛthā vipravaco yastu manyate manujaḥ śubhe //
2.22.d:
विप्रवाक्यं चरेत्सुभ्रु विष्णुस्मरणपूर्वकम् ।
वृथा विप्रवचो यस्तु मन्यते मनुजः शुभे ॥
2.22.m: One should act according to the word of a brāhmaṇa, O fair-browed one, preceded by the remembrance of Viṣṇu. / The mortal who considers a brāhmaṇa's word to be in vain, O fair lady,

2.22.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ naiva dadyādvā sa yāti narakedhruvam /
vratavaikalyamāsādya kuṣṭhī cāndhaḥ prajāyate //
2.22.d:
दक्षिणां नैव दद्याद्वा स याति नरकेध्रुवम् ।
व्रतवैकल्यमासाद्य कुष्ठी चान्धः प्रजायते ॥
2.22.m: Or does not give the priestly gift, certainly goes to hell; / incurring impairment of his vow, he is born a leper and blind.

2.22.s:
dharāmarāṇāṃ vacane vyavasthitā divaukasastīrthagaṇā makhāśca /
ko laṅghayetsubhru vaco hi teṣāṃ śreyobhikāmo manujastu vidvān //
2.22.d:
धरामराणां वचने व्यवस्थिता दिवौकसस्तीर्थगणा मखाश्च ।
को लङ्घयेत्सुभ्रु वचो हि तेषां श्रेयोभिकामो मनुजस्तु विद्वान् ॥
2.22.m: The gods of heaven, hosts of sacred fords, and sacrifices are established upon the word of the gods of the earth; / what wise man desirous of welfare would transgress their word, O fair-browed one?

2.22.s:
idaṃ mayā dharmarahasyayuktaṃ virañcaye śrīpatinā yathoktam /
prakāśitaṃ tubhyamananyavācyaṃ phalapradaṃ mādhavatuṣṭihetum //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge kārtikamāhātmyaṃ nāma dvāviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.22.d:
इदं मया धर्मरहस्ययुक्तं विरञ्चये श्रीपतिना यथोक्तम् ।
प्रकाशितं तुभ्यमनन्यवाच्यं फलप्रदं माधवतुष्टिहेतुम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे कार्तिकमाहात्म्यं नाम द्वाविंशो ऽध्यायः
2.22.m:
This secret doctrine of dharma, as told by the Lord of Śrī to Brahmā, / has been revealed by me to you; it is not to be spoken to anyone else; it bestows fruit and brings delight to Mādhava."

Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled the Eulogy of the Greatness of Kārtika, in the latter section of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.23.s:
mohinyuvāca
vākyamuktaṃ tvayā sādhu kārtike yadupoṣaṇam /
vratādikaraṇaṃ rājñāṃ noktaṃ kvāpi nidarśane //
2.23.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
वाक्यमुक्तं त्वया साधु कार्तिके यदुपोषणम् ।
व्रतादिकरणं राज्ञां नोक्तं क्वापि निदर्शने ॥
2.23.m: Mohinī said: / "A proper statement was spoken by you regarding fasting in Kārtika; / but nowhere in any example has the performance of vows and the like been prescribed for kings.

2.23.s:
muktvaikaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ loke noktaṃ śūdraviśorapi /
dānaṃ hi pālanaṃ yuddhaṃ tṛtīyaṃ bhūbhujāṃ smṛtam //
2.23.d:
मुक्त्वैकं ब्राह्मणं लोके नोक्तं शूद्रविशोरपि ।
दानं हि पालनं युद्धं तृतीयं भूभुजां स्मृतम् ॥
2.23.m: Except for the brāhmaṇa alone, in this world it is not enjoined even for the śūdra and the vaiśya. / Giving gifts, protection, and warfare are remembered as the three duties for kings.

2.23.s:
na vrataṃ hi tvayā kāryaṃ yadi māmicchasi priyām /
muhūrtamapi rājendra na śaknomi tvayā vinā //
2.23.d:
न व्रतं हि त्वया कार्यं यदि मामिच्छसि प्रियाम् ।
मुहूर्तमपि राजेन्द्र न शक्नोमि त्वया विना ॥
2.23.m: Indeed, no vow should be performed by you if you hold me dear. / O king of kings, I cannot endure even a moment without you,

2.23.s:
sthātuṃ kamalagarbhābha kiṃ punarmāsasaṃkhyayā /
yatropavāsakaraṇaṃ manyase vasādhādhipa //
2.23.d:
स्थातुं कमलगर्भाभ किं पुनर्माससंख्यया ।
यत्रोपवासकरणं मन्यसे वसाधाधिप ॥
2.23.m: O lotus-hued one, so what need be said of an entire month? / If you consider fasting to be necessary, O lord of the earth,

2.23.s:
tatra vai bhojanaṃ deyaṃ viprāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām /
athavā jyeṣṭhapatnī yā sā karotu vratādikam /
evamukte tu vacane mohinyā rukmabhūṣaṇaḥ //
2.23.d:
तत्र वै भोजनं देयं विप्राणां च महात्मनाम् ।
अथवा ज्येष्ठपत्नी या सा करोतु व्रतादिकम् ।
एवमुक्ते तु वचने मोहिन्या रुक्मभूषणः ॥
2.23.m: Then food should be given to great-souled brāhmaṇas; / or else let your senior wife perform the vows and the like." / When such words were spoken by Mohinī, the king adorned with gold ornaments

2.23.s:
ājuhāva priyāṃ bhāryāṃ nāmnā saṃdhyāvaliṃśubhām /
āhūtā tatkṣaṇātprāptā rājānaṃ bhūridakṣiṇam //
2.23.d:
आजुहाव प्रियां भार्यां नाम्ना संध्यावलिंशुभाम् ।
आहूता तत्क्षणात्प्राप्ता राजानं भूरिदक्षिणम् ॥
2.23.m: Summoned his beloved and auspicious wife named Saṃdhyāvalī. / Summoned, she arrived at that very moment before the king who bestowed abundant priestly gifts,

2.23.s:
āśīnaṃ śayane divye mohinībāhusaṃvṛtam /
saṃghṛṣṭaṃ hi kucāgreṇa svarṇakuṃbhanibhena hi //
2.23.d:
आशीनं शयने दिव्ये मोहिनीबाहुसंवृतम् ।
संघृष्टं हि कुचाग्रेण स्वर्णकुंभनिभेन हि ॥
2.23.m: Who was seated on a splendid couch, embraced by the arms of Mohinī, / and rubbed against the tips of her breasts that resembled golden jars.

2.23.s:
śayane vāmanetrāyāḥ sakāmāyā mahīpate /
kṛtāṃ jalipuṭā bhūtvā bharturnamitakandharā //
2.23.d:
शयने वामनेत्रायाः सकामाया महीपते ।
कृतां जलिपुटा भूत्वा भर्तुर्नमितकन्धरा ॥
2.23.m: On the couch of that fair-eyed woman full of desire, O king, / folding her hands in reverence and bowing her head to her husband,

2.23.s:
saṃdhyāvalī prāha nṛpaṃ kimāhūtā karomyaham /
tava vākye sthitā kānta duḥsāpatnyavivarjitā //
2.23.d:
संध्यावली प्राह नृपं किमाहूता करोम्यहम् ।
तव वाक्ये स्थिता कान्त दुःसापत्न्यविवर्जिता ॥
2.23.m: Saṃdhyāvalī said to the king: "Having been summoned, what shall I do? / I abide by your command, my beloved, free from hostility toward my co-wife.

2.23.s:
yathā yathā hi ramase mohinyā sahaha bhūpate /
tathā tathā mama prītirvarddhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.23.d:
यथा यथा हि रमसे मोहिन्या सहह भूपते ।
तथा तथा मम प्रीतिर्वर्द्धते नात्र संशयः ॥
2.23.m: The more you take pleasure with Mohinī, O king, / the more my joy increases; of this there is no doubt.

2.23.s:
bhartuḥ saukhyena yā nārī duḥkhayuktā prajāyate /
sā tu śyenī bhavedrājaṃstrīṇi varṣāṇi pañca ca //
2.23.d:
भर्तुः सौख्येन या नारी दुःखयुक्ता प्रजायते ।
सा तु श्येनी भवेद्राजंस्त्रीणि वर्षाणि पञ्च च ॥
2.23.m: A woman who becomes unhappy because of her husband's happiness / becomes a hawk, O king, for eight years.

2.23.s: ājñāṃ me dehi rājendra mā vrīhāṃ kāmikāṃ kuru //
2.23.d: आज्ञां मे देहि राजेन्द्र मा व्रीहां कामिकां कुरु ॥
2.23.m: Give me an order, O king of kings; do not feel ashamed toward your desirous [wife]."

2.23.s:
rukmāṅgada uvāca
jānāmi tava śīlaṃ tu kulaṃ jānāmi bhāmini /
tava vākyena hi ciraṃ mohinī ramitā mayā //
2.23.d:
रुक्माङ्गद उवाच
जानामि तव शीलं तु कुलं जानामि भामिनि ।
तव वाक्येन हि चिरं मोहिनी रमिता मया ॥
2.23.m: Rukmāṅgada said: / "I know your character, O fair lady, and I know your noble lineage. / Indeed, it was by your word that I have long enjoyed pleasure with Mohinī.

2.23.s:
ramamāṇasya suciraṃ bahavaḥ kārtikā gatāḥ /
priyā saukhyena mugdhasya na gato harivāsaraḥ //
2.23.d:
रममाणस्य सुचिरं बहवः कार्तिका गताः ।
प्रिया सौख्येन मुग्धस्य न गतो हरिवासरः ॥
2.23.m: While I was thus sporting for a long time, many Kārtika months have passed; / bewitched by the happiness of my beloved, no day of Hari was observed.

2.23.s:
so 'haṃ tṛptimanuprāptaḥ kāmabhogātpunaḥ punaḥ /
jñāto 'yaṃ kārtiko māsaḥ sarvapāpakṣayaṅkaraḥ //
2.23.d:
सो ऽहं तृप्तिमनुप्राप्तः कामभोगात्पुनः पुनः ।
ज्ञातो ऽयं कार्तिको मासः सर्वपापक्षयङ्करः ॥
2.23.m: I, having obtained satiety through sexual pleasures again and again, / have come to know this month of Kārtika that destroys all sins.

2.23.s:
kartukāmo vrataṃ devi kārtikākhyaṃ supuṇyadam /
iyaṃ vārayate māṃ ca vratādbrahmasutā śubhe //
2.23.d:
कर्तुकामो व्रतं देवि कार्तिकाख्यं सुपुण्यदम् ।
इयं वारयते मां च व्रताद्ब्रह्मसुता शुभे ॥
2.23.m: O queen, desiring to perform the vow named Kārtika that bestows great merit, / I am restrained from the vow by this daughter of Brahmā, O auspicious one.

2.23.s:
asyā na vipriyaṃ kāryaṃ sarvathā varavarṇini /
māmakaṃ vratamādhatsva kṛcchrākhyaṃ kāyaśoṣakam //
2.23.d:
अस्या न विप्रियं कार्यं सर्वथा वरवर्णिनि ।
मामकं व्रतमाधत्स्व कृच्छ्राख्यं कायशोषकम् ॥
2.23.m: What is displeasing to her must not be done by any means, O woman of excellent complexion; / undertake my vow called the kṛcchra penance, which emaciates the body."

2.23.s:
sā caivamuktā navahemavarṇā bhartrā tadā pīnapayodharaṅgī /
uvāca vākyaṃ dvijarājakaktrāvrataṃ cariṣye tava tuṣṭihetoḥ //
2.23.d:
सा चैवमुक्ता नवहेमवर्णा भर्त्रा तदा पीनपयोधरङ्गी ।
उवाच वाक्यं द्विजराजकक्त्राव्रतं चरिष्ये तव तुष्टिहेतोः ॥
2.23.m: She, having the complexion of fresh gold, endowed with full breasts, and possessing a face like the king of the twice-born, / addressed thus by her husband, then spoke these words: "I will perform the vow for the sake of your pleasure.

2.23.s:
yenaiva kīrtistu yaśo bhavecca tathaiva saukhyaṃ tava kīrtiyuktam /
karomi saumyaṃ naradevanātha kṣipāmi dehaṃ jvalanetvadartham //
2.23.d:
येनैव कीर्तिस्तु यशो भवेच्च तथैव सौख्यं तव कीर्तियुक्तम् ।
करोमि सौम्यं नरदेवनाथ क्षिपामि देहं ज्वलनेत्वदर्थम् ॥
2.23.m: Whatever will bring you renown, glory, and happiness accompanied by fame, / that agreeable deed I shall do, O ruler of men; I would even cast my body into the fire for your sake!

2.23.s:
akāryametannahi bhūmipāla vākyena te hanmi sutaṃ svakīyam /
kintvevametadvratakarma bhūyaḥ karomi saumyaṃ naradevanātha //
2.23.d:
अकार्यमेतन्नहि भूमिपाल वाक्येन ते हन्मि सुतं स्वकीयम् ।
किन्त्वेवमेतद्व्रतकर्म भूयः करोमि सौम्यं नरदेवनाथ ॥
2.23.m: This [vow] is not something that should not be done, O protector of the earth; at your word I would even slay my own son! / How much more, then, this sacred act of a vow: I shall perform it, O gentle lord of men!"

2.23.s:
ityevamuktvā raviputraśatruṃ praṇamya taṃ cāruviśālanetrā /
vrataṃ cakārātha tadā hi devī hyaśeṣapāpaughavināśanāya //
2.23.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा रविपुत्रशत्रुं प्रणम्य तं चारुविशालनेत्रा ।
व्रतं चकाराथ तदा हि देवी ह्यशेषपापौघविनाशनाय ॥
2.23.m: Having spoken thus and bowed to the enemy of the son of the Sun, that goddess of lovely wide eyes / then undertook the vow for the destruction of the entire multitude of sins.

2.23.s:
vrate pravṛtte varakṛcchrasaṃjñe priyākṛte harṣamavāpa rājā /
uvāca vākyaṃ kuśaketuputrīṃ kṛtaṃ vacaḥ subhru samīhitaṃ te //
2.23.d:
व्रते प्रवृत्ते वरकृच्छ्रसंज्ञे प्रियाकृते हर्षमवाप राजा ।
उवाच वाक्यं कुशकेतुपुत्रीं कृतं वचः सुभ्रु समीहितं ते ॥
2.23.m: When the vow known as the excellent kṛcchra was undertaken by his beloved, the king felt joy; / he spoke these words to the daughter of Kuśaketu: "Your desired word has been fulfilled, O fair-browed one!

2.23.s:
ramasva kāmaṃ maya sanniviṣṭasaṃpūrṇavāñchā karabhoru hṛṣṭā /
vimuktakāryastava subhru hetornānyāsti nārī mama saukhyahetuḥ //
2.23.d:
रमस्व कामं मय सन्निविष्टसंपूर्णवाञ्छा करभोरु हृष्टा ।
विमुक्तकार्यस्तव सुभ्रु हेतोर्नान्यास्ति नारी मम सौख्यहेतुः ॥
2.23.m: Delight to your heart's content, your desires completely fulfilled through me, O woman with thighs like an elephant's trunk, rejoice! / Free from obligations for your sake, O fair-browed one, no other woman is the cause of my happiness."

2.23.s:
sā tvevamuktā nijanāyakena praharṣamabhyetya jagāda bhūpam /
jñātvā bhavantaṃ bahukāmayuktaṃ triviṣṭapānnātha samāgatāham //
2.23.d:
सा त्वेवमुक्ता निजनायकेन प्रहर्षमभ्येत्य जगाद भूपम् ।
ज्ञात्वा भवन्तं बहुकामयुक्तं त्रिविष्टपान्नाथ समागताहम् ॥
2.23.m: She, thus addressed by her lover, felt immense joy and spoke to the king: / "Knowing you to be filled with deep desire, O lord, I have come from heaven,

2.23.s:
tyaktvāmarāndaityagaṇāṃśca sarvāngandharvayakṣoragarākṣasāṃśca /
saṃdṛśyamānānmama nātha hetoḥ snehānvitāhaṃ tava mandarādrau //
2.23.d:
त्यक्त्वामरान्दैत्यगणांश्च सर्वान्गन्धर्वयक्षोरगराक्षसांश्च ।
संदृश्यमानान्मम नाथ हेतोः स्नेहान्विताहं तव मन्दराद्रौ ॥
2.23.m: Having forsaken all the immortals, the hosts of daityas, gandharvas, yakṣas, uragas, and rākṣasas, / who were gazing upon me, O lord; out of affection I have come to you on Mount Mandara.

2.23.s:
etatkāmaphalaṃ loke yaddvayorekacittatā /
anyacetaḥ kṛtaḥ kāmaḥ śavayoriva saṃgamaḥ //
2.23.d:
एतत्कामफलं लोके यद्द्वयोरेकचित्तता ।
अन्यचेतः कृतः कामः शवयोरिव संगमः ॥
2.23.m: This is the fruit of love in this world: that two persons share a single heart; / love made with divided hearts is like the union of two corpses.

2.23.s:
saphalaṃ hi vapurme 'dya saphalaṃ rūpameva hi /
tvayā kāmavatā kānta durllabhaṃ yajjagattraye //
2.23.d:
सफलं हि वपुर्मे ऽद्य सफलं रूपमेव हि ।
त्वया कामवता कान्त दुर्ल्लभं यज्जगत्त्रये ॥
2.23.m: Fruitful indeed is my body today! Fruitful indeed is my beauty! / United with you who are filled with passion, O beloved, a fortune hard to attain in the three worlds!

2.23.s:
pronnatābhyāṃ kucābhyāṃ hi kāmino hṛdayaṃ yadi /
saṃśliṣṭaṃ nahi śīryeta manye vajrasamaṃ dṛḍham /
tadeva cāmṛtaṃ loke yatpurandhryadharāsavam //
2.23.d:
प्रोन्नताभ्यां कुचाभ्यां हि कामिनो हृदयं यदि ।
संश्लिष्टं नहि शीर्येत मन्ये वज्रसमं दृढम् ।
तदेव चामृतं लोके यत्पुरन्ध्र्यधरासवम् ॥
2.23.m: If a lover's heart embraced by high, swelling breasts does not shatter, / I consider it firm as a diamond! / That alone is the true nectar in the world: the nectar of a fair woman's lower lip,

2.23.s:
kucābhyāṃ hṛdi līnābhyāṃ mukhena paripīyate /
evamuktvā pariṣvajya rājānaṃ rahasi sthitam //
2.23.d:
कुचाभ्यां हृदि लीनाभ्यां मुखेन परिपीयते ।
एवमुक्त्वा परिष्वज्य राजानं रहसि स्थितम् ॥
2.23.m: Which is drunk eagerly by the mouth while her breasts cling to his chest." / Having spoken thus and embraced the king who was in private,

2.23.s:
ramayāmāsa tanvaṅgī vātsyāyanavidhānataḥ /
tasyaivaṃ ramamāṇasya mohinyā sahitasya hi //
2.23.d:
रमयामास तन्वङ्गी वात्स्यायनविधानतः ।
तस्यैवं रममाणस्य मोहिन्या सहितस्य हि ॥
2.23.m: The slender-limbed woman made love to him according to the precepts of Vātsyāyana. / While he was thus sporting together with Mohinī,

2.23.s:
rukmāṅgadasya karṇābhyāṃ paṭahadhvanirāgataḥ /
mattebhakuṃbhasaṃsthastu dharmāṅgadanideśataḥ //
2.23.d:
रुक्माङ्गदस्य कर्णाभ्यां पटहध्वनिरागतः ।
मत्तेभकुंभसंस्थस्तु धर्माङ्गदनिदेशतः ॥
2.23.m: The sound of a war-drum reached Rukmāṅgada's ears, / beaten upon the forehead of a rutting elephant by the command of Dharmāṅgada.

2.23.s:
prātarharidinaṃ lokāstiṣṭhadhvaṃ tvekabhojanāḥ /
akṣāralavaṇāḥ sarve haviṣyānnaniṣeviṇaḥ //
2.23.d:
प्रातर्हरिदिनं लोकास्तिष्ठध्वं त्वेकभोजनाः ।
अक्षारलवणाः सर्वे हविष्यान्ननिषेविणः ॥
2.23.m: "Tomorrow is the day of Hari! O people, remain taking only one meal, / all of you eating haviṣya food, free from pungents and salt,

2.23.s:
avanītalpaśayanāḥ priyāsaṃgavivarjitāḥ /
smaradhvaṃ devadeveśaṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣottamam //
2.23.d:
अवनीतल्पशयनाः प्रियासंगविवर्जिताः ।
स्मरध्वं देवदेवेशं पुराणं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
2.23.m: sleeping on a bed on the bare ground, abstaining from intimacy with a beloved! / Remember the ancient Supreme Person, the Lord of the god of gods!

2.23.s:
sakṛdbhojanasaṃyuktā upavāsaṃ kariṣyatha /
akṛtaśrāddhanicayā aprāptāḥ piṇḍameva ca //
2.23.d:
सकृद्भोजनसंयुक्ता उपवासं करिष्यथ ।
अकृतश्राद्धनिचया अप्राप्ताः पिण्डमेव च ॥
2.23.m: Having taken but one meal, you shall observe a fast. / Those who have not performed a heap of ancestral rites and have not obtained an ancestral rice-ball,

2.23.s:
gayāmagataputrāśca gacchadhvaṃ śrīhareḥ padam /
eṣā kārtikaśuklā vai harernidrāvyapohinī //
2.23.d:
गयामगतपुत्राश्च गच्छध्वं श्रीहरेः पदम् ।
एषा कार्तिकशुक्ला वै हरेर्निद्राव्यपोहिनी ॥
2.23.m: and those whose sons have not gone to Gayā, go to the abode of glorious Hari! / This bright fortnight of Kārttika is indeed that which dispels the sleep of Hari.

2.23.s:
prātarekādaśī prāptā mā kṛthā bhojanaṃ kvacit /
brahmahatyādipāpāni kāmakārakṛtāni ca //
2.23.d:
प्रातरेकादशी प्राप्ता मा कृथा भोजनं क्वचित् ।
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि कामकारकृतानि च ॥
2.23.m: Tomorrow ekādaśī has arrived; do not take food anywhere! / Sins such as the murder of a brahmin and those committed intentionally—

2.23.s:
tāni yāsyanti sarvāṇi upoṣyemāṃ prabodhinīm /
prabodhayeddharmmaparānnyāyācāra samanvitān //
2.23.d:
तानि यास्यन्ति सर्वाणि उपोष्येमां प्रबोधिनीम् ।
प्रबोधयेद्धर्म्मपरान्न्यायाचार समन्वितान् ॥
2.23.m: all those will depart by fasting on this Prabodhinī. / It awakens those dedicated to dharma who possess righteous conduct.

2.23.s:
hareḥ prabodhamādhatte tenaiṣā bodhinī smṛtā /
sakṛccopoṣitāṃ cemāṃ nidrācchedakarīṃ hareḥ //
2.23.d:
हरेः प्रबोधमाधत्ते तेनैषा बोधिनी स्मृता ।
सकृच्चोपोषितां चेमां निद्राच्छेदकरीं हरेः ॥
2.23.m: It brings about the awakening of Hari; therefore it is called Bodhinī. / If one has fasted even once on this day which ends the sleep of Hari,

2.23.s:
tanayo na bhavenmartyo na garbhe jāyate punaḥ /
rurudhvaṃ cakriṇaḥ pūjāmātmavittena mānavāḥ //
2.23.d:
तनयो न भवेन्मर्त्यो न गर्भे जायते पुनः ।
रुरुध्वं चक्रिणः पूजामात्मवित्तेन मानवाः ॥
2.23.m: one's son will not remain a mortal, nor is one born again in a womb. / O men, perform the worship of the wielder of the discus with your own wealth!

2.23.s:
vastraiḥ puṣpairdhūpadīpairvaracandanakuṅkumaiḥ /
suhṛdyaiśca phalairgandhairyajadhvaṃ śrīhareḥ padam //
2.23.d:
वस्त्रैः पुष्पैर्धूपदीपैर्वरचन्दनकुङ्कुमैः ।
सुहृद्यैश्च फलैर्गन्धैर्यजध्वं श्रीहरेः पदम् ॥
2.23.m: Worship the abode of glorious Hari with garments, flowers, incenses, lamps, / excellent sandalpaste, saffron, delightful fruits, and fragrant perfumes!

2.23.s:
yo na kuryādvaco me 'dya dharmyaṃ viṣṇugatipradam /
sa me daṇḍyaśca vādhyaśca nirvāsyo viṣayāddhruvam //
2.23.d:
यो न कुर्याद्वचो मे ऽद्य धर्म्यं विष्णुगतिप्रदम् ।
स मे दण्ड्यश्च वाध्यश्च निर्वास्यो विषयाद्ध्रुवम् ॥
2.23.m: Whoever does not carry out my righteous word today, which grants the state of Viṣṇu, / must certainly be punished by me, executed, and banished from my domain!"

2.23.s:
evaṃvidhe vādyamāne paṭahe meghaniḥsvane /
hastā damuñca tāṃbūlaṃ sakarpūraṃ nṛpottamaḥ //
2.23.d:
एवंविधे वाद्यमाने पटहे मेघनिःस्वने ।
हस्ता दमुञ्च तांबूलं सकर्पूरं नृपोत्तमः ॥
2.23.m: While such a proclamation-drum sounding like a cloud was being beaten, / the best of kings dropped the betel with camphor from his hand.

2.23.s:
mohinīkucayorlagnaṃ hṛdayaṃ sa vikṛṣya vai /
udattiṣṭhanmahīpālaḥ śayyāyāṃ rativarddhanaḥ //
2.23.d:
मोहिनीकुचयोर्लग्नं हृदयं स विकृष्य वै ।
उदत्तिष्ठन्महीपालः शय्यायां रतिवर्द्धनः ॥
2.23.m: Withdrawing his heart that was attached to Mohinī's breasts, / the protector of the earth, who was augmenting pleasure, rose from the bed.

2.23.s:
mohinīṃ mohakāmārttāṃ satviyan ślakṣṇayā girā /
devi prātarharidinaṃ bhaviṣyatyadhanāśanam //
2.23.d:
मोहिनीं मोहकामार्त्तां सत्वियन् श्लक्ष्णया गिरा ।
देवि प्रातर्हरिदिनं भविष्यत्यधनाशनम् ॥
2.23.m: Comforting Mohinī, who was afflicted by bewildering desire, with gentle words, [he said]: / "O queen, tomorrow is the day of Hari, when food should be eaten at midday.

2.23.s:
saṃyato 'haṃ bhaviṣyāmi kṣamyatāṃ kṣamyatāmiti /
tavājñayā mayā kṛcchraṃ sandhyāvalyā tu kāritam //
2.23.d:
संयतो ऽहं भविष्यामि क्षम्यतां क्षम्यतामिति ।
तवाज्ञया मया कृच्छ्रं सन्ध्यावल्या तु कारितम् ॥
2.23.m: I shall be self-restrained; forgive me, forgive me! / By your command, the hard penance was indeed caused to be performed by Sandhyāvalī.

2.23.s:
iyamekādaśī kāryā prabodhakaraṇī mayā /
aśeṣapāpabandhasya chedanī gatidāyinī //
2.23.d:
इयमेकादशी कार्या प्रबोधकरणी मया ।
अशेषपापबन्धस्य छेदनी गतिदायिनी ॥
2.23.m: This ekādaśī, which brings about awakening, must be observed by me; / it cuts off the entire bond of sins and grants the [highest] path,

2.23.s:
trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ mahotsavavidhāyinī /
tasmāddhaviṣyaṃ bhokṣye 'haṃ niyato mattagāminī //
2.23.d:
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां महोत्सवविधायिनी ।
तस्माद्धविष्यं भोक्ष्ये ऽहं नियतो मत्तगामिनी ॥
2.23.m: bringing about a great festival even for the three worlds. / Therefore, O woman of graceful gait, I shall eat haviṣya food, being self-controlled.

2.23.s:
mayā saha viśālākṣi tvaṃ cāpi tamadhokṣajam /
ārādhaya hṛṣīkeśamupavāsaparāyaṇā /
yena yāsyasi nirvāṇaṃ dāhapralayavarjitam //
2.23.d:
मया सह विशालाक्षि त्वं चापि तमधोक्षजम् ।
आराधय हृषीकेशमुपवासपरायणा ।
येन यास्यसि निर्वाणं दाहप्रलयवर्जितम् ॥
2.23.m: Together with me, O large-eyed one, you too worship Adhokṣaja, / Hṛṣīkeśa, being devoted to the fast, / by which you will go to nirvāṇa, free from burning and dissolution."

2.23.s:
mohinyuvāca
sādhūktaṃ hi tvayā rājanpūjanaṃ cakrapāṇinaḥ /
janmamṛtyujarāchedi kariṣye 'haṃ tavājñayā //
2.23.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
साधूक्तं हि त्वया राजन्पूजनं चक्रपाणिनः ।
जन्ममृत्युजराछेदि करिष्ये ऽहं तवाज्ञया ॥
2.23.m: Mohinī said: / "Well spoken indeed by you, O king! Worship of the wielder of the discus / cuts off birth, death, and old age; I shall perform it by your command.

2.23.s:
pratijñā yā tvayā pūrvaṃ kṛtā mandaramastake /
karapradānasahitā bhavatā sukṛtāṅkitā //
2.23.d:
प्रतिज्ञा या त्वया पूर्वं कृता मन्दरमस्तके ।
करप्रदानसहिता भवता सुकृताङ्किता ॥
2.23.m: The vow that was made by you earlier upon the summit of Mandara, / accompanied by the giving of your hand and sealed by your merit—

2.23.s:
tasyāstu samayaḥ prāpto dīyatāṃ sa hi me tvayā /
janmaprabhṛti yatpuṇyaṃ tvayā yatnena saṃcitam //
2.23.d:
तस्यास्तु समयः प्राप्तो दीयतां स हि मे त्वया ।
जन्मप्रभृति यत्पुण्यं त्वया यत्नेन संचितम् ॥
2.23.m: the time for that has indeed arrived; let it be granted to me by you! / Whatever merit has been accumulated with effort by you since birth,

2.23.s:
tatsarvaṃ naśyati kṣipraṃ na dadāsi varaṃ yadi /
rukmāṅgada uvāca
ehi cārvaṅgi karttāsmi yatte manasi vartate //
2.23.d:
तत्सर्वं नश्यति क्षिप्रं न ददासि वरं यदि ।
रुक्माङ्गद उवाच
एहि चार्वङ्गि कर्त्तास्मि यत्ते मनसि वर्तते ॥
2.23.m: all that will perish quickly if you do not grant the boon." / Rukmāṅgada said: / "Come, O beautiful-limbed one, I will do whatever is in your mind.

2.23.s:
nādeyaṃ vidyate kiñcittubhyaṃ me jīvitāvadhi /
kiṃ punargrāmavittādi dharāyuktaṃ ca bhāmini //
2.23.d:
नादेयं विद्यते किञ्चित्तुभ्यं मे जीवितावधि ।
किं पुनर्ग्रामवित्तादि धरायुक्तं च भामिनि ॥
2.23.m: Nothing exists that cannot be given by me to you up to the limit of my life, / what to speak of villages, wealth, and the like, together with the earth, O splendid woman!"

2.23.s:
mohinyuvāca
nātha kānta vibho rājan jīviteśa ratipriya /
nopoṣyaṃ vāmaraṃ viṣṇorbhoktavyā yadyahaṃ priyā //
2.23.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
नाथ कान्त विभो राजन् जीवितेश रतिप्रिय ।
नोपोष्यं वामरं विष्णोर्भोक्तव्या यद्यहं प्रिया ॥
2.23.m: Mohinī said: / "O lord, O beloved, O master, O king, O lord of my life, O lover of pleasure! / The day of Viṣṇu is not to be fasted, and I am to be enjoyed if I am dear [to you].

2.23.s:
na ca te 'haṃ priyā rājan suhūrtamapi kāmaye /
tvatsaṃyogaṃ vinā bhūtā bhaviṣyāmi varaṃ vinā //
2.23.d:
न च ते ऽहं प्रिया राजन् सुहूर्तमपि कामये ।
त्वत्संयोगं विना भूता भविष्यामि वरं विना ॥
2.23.m: If I am not dear to you, O king, I do not desire even a moment [with you]; / remaining without union with you, I shall be without the boon.

2.23.s:
tasmānmāṃ yadi vāñchethā bhoktuṃ satyaparāyaṇa /
tadā tyajopavāsaṃ hi bhujyatāṃ harivāsare //
2.23.d:
तस्मान्मां यदि वाञ्छेथा भोक्तुं सत्यपरायण ।
तदा त्यजोपवासं हि भुज्यतां हरिवासरे ॥
2.23.m: Therefore, if you wish to enjoy me, O devotee of truth, / then give up the fast and let food be eaten on the day of Hari!

2.23.s:
eṣa eva varo deyo yo mayā prārthitaḥ purā /
na ceddāsyasi rājendra bhūtvānṛtavacābhavān //
2.23.d:
एष एव वरो देयो यो मया प्रार्थितः पुरा ।
न चेद्दास्यसि राजेन्द्र भूत्वानृतवचाभवान् ॥
2.23.m: This very boon must be given, which was requested by me formerly. / If you do not grant it, O king of kings, you, having become a speaker of falsehood,

2.23.s:
yāsyate narake ghore yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam /
rājovāca
maivaṃ tvaṃ vada kalyāṇi nedaṃ tvayyupapadyate //
2.23.d:
यास्यते नरके घोरे यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ।
राजोवाच
मैवं त्वं वद कल्याणि नेदं त्वय्युपपद्यते ॥
2.23.m: shall go to a dreadful hell until the dissolution of all beings." / The king said: / "Do not speak thus, O auspicious one! This is not proper for you.

2.23.s:
vidheśca tanayā bhūtvā dharmavighnaṃ koroṣi kim /
janmaprabhṛtyahaṃ naiva bhuktavānharivāsare //
2.23.d:
विधेश्च तनया भूत्वा धर्मविघ्नं कोरोषि किम् ।
जन्मप्रभृत्यहं नैव भुक्तवान्हरिवासरे ॥
2.23.m: Having been born as the daughter of Brahmā, why do you cause an obstacle to dharma? / Since birth I have never eaten on the day of Hari.

2.23.s:
sa cādyāhaṃ kathaṃ bhoktā saṃjātapalitaḥ śubhe /
yauvanātītamartyasya kṣīṇendriyabalasya ca //
2.23.d:
स चाद्याहं कथं भोक्ता संजातपलितः शुभे ।
यौवनातीतमर्त्यस्य क्षीणेन्द्रियबलस्य च ॥
2.23.m: How can that same I eat today, having grown grey hairs, O auspicious woman? / For a mortal past his youth, whose sensory strength is diminished,

2.23.s:
svarṇadīsevanaṃ yuktamathavā haripūjanam /
na kṛtaṃ yanmayā bālye yauvane na kṛtaṃ ca yat //
2.23.d:
स्वर्णदीसेवनं युक्तमथवा हरिपूजनम् ।
न कृतं यन्मया बाल्ये यौवने न कृतं च यत् ॥
2.23.m: resorting to the golden river [Gaṅgā] or worshiping Hari is appropriate. / What was not done by me in childhood, and what was not done in youth,

2.23.s:
tadahaṃ kṣīṇavīryo 'dya kathaṃ kuryāṃ jugupsitam /
prasīda capalāpāṅgi prasīda varavarṇini //
2.23.d:
तदहं क्षीणवीर्यो ऽद्य कथं कुर्यां जुगुप्सितम् ।
प्रसीद चपलापाङ्गि प्रसीद वरवर्णिनि ॥
2.23.m: how can I, now lacking vigor, do that detestable thing today? / Be gracious, O woman of darting glances! Be gracious, O woman of excellent complexion!

2.23.s:
mā kuruṣva vrate bhaṅgaṃ dātāhaṃ rājyasaṃpadām /
athavā necchasi tvaṃ tatkaromyanyatsulocane //
2.23.d:
मा कुरुष्व व्रते भङ्गं दाताहं राज्यसंपदाम् ।
अथवा नेच्छसि त्वं तत्करोम्यन्यत्सुलोचने ॥
2.23.m: Do not break my observance! I will give the riches of the kingdom, / or, if you do not desire that, I shall do something else, O fair-eyed one!

2.23.s:
āropayitvā śibikāṃ vimānapratimāṃ śubhām /
yatrecchasi nayiṣyāmi pādacārī kalatrayuk //
2.23.d:
आरोपयित्वा शिबिकां विमानप्रतिमां शुभाम् ।
यत्रेच्छसि नयिष्यामि पादचारी कलत्रयुक् ॥
2.23.m: Having placed [you] in a palanquin resembling an auspicious celestial chariot, / I, accompanied by my wife, will carry you on foot wherever you desire.

2.23.s:
yadi taccāpi necchestvaṃ vimānaṃ hi kṛtaṃ mayā /
tarhi svarṇamayau staṃbhau kṛtvā vidrumabhūṣitau //
2.23.d:
यदि तच्चापि नेच्छेस्त्वं विमानं हि कृतं मया ।
तर्हि स्वर्णमयौ स्तंभौ कृत्वा विद्रुमभूषितौ ॥
2.23.m: If you do not desire even that celestial chariot made by me, / then, having erected two golden pillars adorned with coral,

2.23.s:
muktāphalamayīṃ dolāṃ kariṣye tvatkṛte priye /
tatra tvāṃ dolayiṣyāmi bahūnmāsānaharniśam //
2.23.d:
मुक्ताफलमयीं दोलां करिष्ये त्वत्कृते प्रिये ।
तत्र त्वां दोलयिष्यामि बहून्मासानहर्निशम् ॥
2.23.m: I will make a swing made of pearls for your sake, my beloved. / There I will swing you for many months, day and night.

2.23.s:
vratabhaṅgaṃ varārohe mā kuruṣva mama priye /
varaṃ śvapacamāṃsaṃ hi śvamāṃsaṃ vā varānane //
2.23.d:
व्रतभङ्गं वरारोहे मा कुरुष्व मम प्रिये ।
वरं श्वपचमांसं हि श्वमांसं वा वरानने ॥
2.23.m: O woman of lovely hips, do not cause the breaking of my observance, O my beloved! / It would be better indeed for men to eat dog-cooker's flesh, or dog's meat, O fair-faced one,

2.23.s:
ātmano vā narairbhuktaṃ yairbhuktaṃ harivāsare /
trailokyaghātinaḥ pāpaṃ maithune śaśinaḥ kṣaye //
2.23.d:
आत्मनो वा नरैर्भुक्तं यैर्भुक्तं हरिवासरे ।
त्रैलोक्यघातिनः पापं मैथुने शशिनः क्षये ॥
2.23.m: or their own flesh, than what is eaten by those who have eaten on the day of Hari! / The sin of a slayer of the three worlds enters into a man

2.23.s:
narasya saṃcaretpāpaṃ bhūtāyāṃ kṣaurakarmaṇi /
bhojane vāsare viṣṇostaile ṣaṣṭyāṃ vyavasthite //
2.23.d:
नरस्य संचरेत्पापं भूतायां क्षौरकर्मणि ।
भोजने वासरे विष्णोस्तैले षष्ट्यां व्यवस्थिते ॥
2.23.m: in sexual intercourse during the waning of the moon, in the act of shaving on the fourteenth lunar day, / in eating on the day of Viṣṇu, when oil is used on the sixth lunar day,

2.23.s:
lavaṇe tu tṛtīyāyāṃ saptamyāṃ piśite śubhe /
ājyeṣu paurṇamāsyāṃ vai surāyāṃ ravisaṃkrame //
2.23.d:
लवणे तु तृतीयायां सप्तम्यां पिशिते शुभे ।
आज्येषु पौर्णमास्यां वै सुरायां रविसंक्रमे ॥
2.23.m: in salt on the third, in meat on the seventh, O auspicious one, / in clarified butter on the full moon day, in liquor at the sun's ingress into a zodiac sign,

2.23.s:
gocārasya pralope ca kūṭasākṣyapradāyake /
nikṣepahārake vāpi kumārīvighnakārake //
2.23.d:
गोचारस्य प्रलोपे च कूटसाक्ष्यप्रदायके ।
निक्षेपहारके वापि कुमारीविघ्नकारके ॥
2.23.m: in destroying pasture land, in giving false testimony, / in stealing a deposit, or in hindering an unmarried maiden,

2.23.s:
viśvastaghātake cāpi mṛtavatsāpradogdhari /
dadāmīti dvijāgryāya pratiśrutya na dātari //
2.23.d:
विश्वस्तघातके चापि मृतवत्साप्रदोग्धरि ।
ददामीति द्विजाग्र्याय प्रतिश्रुत्य न दातरि ॥
2.23.m: in betraying one who trusts, in milking a cow whose calf is dead, / in promising 'I will give' to the best of brahmins and not giving,

2.23.s:
maṇikūṭe tulākūṭe kanyānṛtagavānṛte /
yatpātakaṃ tadanne hi saṃsthitaṃ harivāsare //
2.23.d:
मणिकूटे तुलाकूटे कन्यानृतगवानृते ।
यत्पातकं तदन्ने हि संस्थितं हरिवासरे ॥
2.23.m: in falsifying jewels, in falsifying balances, in lying about a maiden, in lying about a cow— / whatever sin there is, it resides in food on the day of Hari!

2.23.s:
tadvidvāṃścārunayane kathaṃ bhokṣyāmi tāpakam /
mohinyuvāca
ekabhuktena naktena tathaivāyācitena ca //
2.23.d:
तद्विद्वांश्चारुनयने कथं भोक्ष्यामि तापकम् ।
मोहिन्युवाच
एकभुक्तेन नक्तेन तथैवायाचितेन च ॥
2.23.m: Knowing that, O fair-eyed one, how shall I eat that which causes torment?" / Mohinī said: / "By eating once, by eating at night, or likewise by eating unasked food,

2.23.s:
upavāsena rājendra dvādaśīṃ na hi laṅghayet /
gurviṇīnāṃ gṛhasthānāṃ kṣīṇānāṃ rogiṇāṃ tathā //
2.23.d:
उपवासेन राजेन्द्र द्वादशीं न हि लङ्घयेत् ।
गुर्विणीनां गृहस्थानां क्षीणानां रोगिणां तथा ॥
2.23.m: or by fasting, O king of kings, one should never transgress dvādaśī. / For pregnant women, householders, the emaciated, and the sick,

2.23.s:
śiśūnāṃ valigātrāṇāṃ na yuktaṃ samupoṣaṇam /
yajñabhogodyatānāṃ ca saṃgrāmakṣitisevinām //
2.23.d:
शिशूनां वलिगात्राणां न युक्तं समुपोषणम् ।
यज्ञभोगोद्यतानां च संग्रामक्षितिसेविनाम् ॥
2.23.m: for children, and for those with wrinkled limbs, complete fasting is not suitable; / and for those engaged in the enjoyment of sacrifices, and those who serve on the battlefield,

2.23.s:
pativratānāṃ rājendra na yuktaṃ samupoṣaṇam /
etanme gautamaḥ prāha sthitāyā mandarācale //
2.23.d:
पतिव्रतानां राजेन्द्र न युक्तं समुपोषणम् ।
एतन्मे गौतमः प्राह स्थिताया मन्दराचले ॥
2.23.m: and for women devoted to their husbands, O king of kings, complete fasting is not suitable. / This was told to me by Gautama while I was staying on Mount Mandara.

2.23.s:
nāvratena dinaṃ viṣṇorneyaṃ manujasattama /
te gṛhasthā dvijā jñeyā yeṣāmagniparigrahaḥ //
2.23.d:
नाव्रतेन दिनं विष्णोर्नेयं मनुजसत्तम ।
ते गृहस्था द्विजा ज्ञेया येषामग्निपरिग्रहः ॥
2.23.m: The day of Viṣṇu should not be spent without an observance, O best of men. / Those twice-born who maintain the sacred fires are to be known as householders.

2.23.s:
rājānaste tu vijñeyā ye prajāpālane sthitāḥ /
gurviṇī hyaṣṭamamāsīyā śiśavaścāṣṭavatsarāḥ //
2.23.d:
राजानस्ते तु विज्ञेया ये प्रजापालने स्थिताः ।
गुर्विणी ह्यष्टममासीया शिशवश्चाष्टवत्सराः ॥
2.23.m: And they are to be known as kings who stand firm in protecting their subjects. / Pregnant women in their eighth month, children up to eight years old,

2.23.s:
atilaṅghaninaḥ kṣīṇā valigātrāstu vārddhakāḥ /
ye vivāhādimāṅgalyakarmavyagrā mahotsavāḥ //
2.23.d:
अतिलङ्घनिनः क्षीणा वलिगात्रास्तु वार्द्धकाः ।
ये विवाहादिमाङ्गल्यकर्मव्यग्रा महोत्सवाः ॥
2.23.m: those exhausted by excessive fasting, the emaciated, and the elderly whose limbs are wrinkled, / those engaged in auspicious rites such as weddings, and those holding great festivals,

2.23.s:
nivṛttāśca pravṛttebhyo yajñānāṃ codyatā hi te /
trividhena purāṇena bhartturyā strī hite ratā //
2.23.d:
निवृत्ताश्च प्रवृत्तेभ्यो यज्ञानां चोद्यता हि ते ।
त्रिविधेन पुराणेन भर्त्तुर्या स्त्री हिते रता ॥
2.23.m: and those who have turned away from worldly engagements and are intent on sacrifices— / according to the threefold Purāṇa, the woman who is devoted to the welfare of her husband,

2.23.s:
pativratā tu sā jñeyā yonisaṃrakṣaṇā tathā /
kimanyairbahubhirbhūpa vākyālāpakṛtairmayā //
2.23.d:
पतिव्रता तु सा ज्ञेया योनिसंरक्षणा तथा ।
किमन्यैर्बहुभिर्भूप वाक्यालापकृतैर्मया ॥
2.23.m: she is to be known as a devoted wife, as is she who guards her chastity. / What need is there, O king, for many other words uttered by me?

2.23.s:
bhojane tu kṛte prītirekādaśyāṃ tvayā mama /
na prītiryadi me chitvā śiraḥ svaṃ hi prayacchasi //
2.23.d:
भोजने तु कृते प्रीतिरेकादश्यां त्वया मम ।
न प्रीतिर्यदि मे छित्वा शिरः स्वं हि प्रयच्छसि ॥
2.23.m: My pleasure is only achieved if you eat on Ekādaśī; / if not my pleasure, then cut off your own head and give it to me!

2.23.s:
na kariṣyasi cedrājan bhojanaṃ harivāsare /
tadā hyasatyavacaso dehaṃ na sparśayāmi te //
2.23.d:
न करिष्यसि चेद्राजन् भोजनं हरिवासरे ।
तदा ह्यसत्यवचसो देहं न स्पर्शयामि ते ॥
2.23.m: If you do not eat on Hari’s day, O king, / then, as a speaker of untruth, I shall not let you touch my body.

2.23.s:
varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ hi satyaṃ rājendra pūjyate /
viśeṣādbhūmipālānāṃ tvadvidhānāṃ mahīpate //
2.23.d:
वर्णानामाश्रमाणां हि सत्यं राजेन्द्र पूज्यते ।
विशेषाद्भूमिपालानां त्वद्विधानां महीपते ॥
2.23.m: Truth indeed is revered among all classes and stages of life, O best of kings, / especially among rulers of the earth such as you, O lord of the earth.

2.23.s:
satyena sūryastapati śaśī satyenarājate /
satye sthitā kṣitirbhūpa satyaṃ dhārayate jagat //
2.23.d:
सत्येन सूर्यस्तपति शशी सत्येनराजते ।
सत्ये स्थिता क्षितिर्भूप सत्यं धारयते जगत् ॥
2.23.m: By truth the sun gives heat; by truth the moon shines bright; / the earth rests upon truth, O king; truth upholds the world.

2.23.s:
satyena vāyurvahati satyena jvalate śikhī /
satyā dhāramidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam //
2.23.d:
सत्येन वायुर्वहति सत्येन ज्वलते शिखी ।
सत्या धारमिदं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
2.23.m: By truth the wind blows; by truth the fire blazes; / this entire universe, both motionless and moving, has truth as its foundation.

2.23.s:
na satyāccālate siṃdhurna vindhyo varddhate nṛpa /
na garbhaṃ yuvatī dhatte velātītaṃ kadācana //
2.23.d:
न सत्याच्चालते सिंधुर्न विन्ध्यो वर्द्धते नृप ।
न गर्भं युवती धत्ते वेलातीतं कदाचन ॥
2.23.m: The ocean does not transgress [its bounds] because of truth, nor does Mount Vindhya grow, O king; / a young woman never bears a child past its due time [because of truth].

2.23.s:
satye sthitā hi taravaḥ phalapuṣpapradarśinaḥ /
divyādisādhanaṃ nṝṇāṃ satyādhāraṃ mahīpate //
2.23.d:
सत्ये स्थिता हि तरवः फलपुष्पप्रदर्शिनः ।
दिव्यादिसाधनं नॄणां सत्याधारं महीपते ॥
2.23.m: Firm in truth, the trees show forth flowers and fruit; / the means to heaven and the like for men is founded upon truth, O lord of the earth.

2.23.s:
aśvamedhasahasrebhyaḥ satyameva viśiṣyate /
madirāpānatulyena karmaṇā lipyase 'nṛtāt //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇottarabhāge rukmāṅgadasaṃlāpo nāma trayoviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.23.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्रेभ्यः सत्यमेव विशिष्यते ।
मदिरापानतुल्येन कर्मणा लिप्यसे ऽनृतात् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणोत्तरभागे रुक्माङ्गदसंलापो नाम त्रयोविंशो ऽध्यायः
2.23.m:
Truth is superior even to thousands of horse-sacrifices; / from untruth you will be tainted with an act equal to drinking wine.

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named 'The Dialogue of Rukmāṅgada', in the latter section of the venerable Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

2.24.s:
rājovāca
yattvayā vyāhṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mamedaṃ gautameritam /
mandare parvataśreṣṭhe harivāsarabhojanam //
2.24.d:
राजोवाच
यत्त्वया व्याहृतं वाक्यं ममेदं गौतमेरितम् ।
मन्दरे पर्वतश्रेष्ठे हरिवासरभोजनम् ॥
2.24.m: The king said: / As to the word spoken by you to me, which was uttered by Gautama / on Mount Mandara, the foremost of mountains, regarding eating on Hari’s day—

2.24.s:
amatena purāṇānāṃ vyāhṛtaṃ yaddvijanmanā /
kṣudraśāstropadeśena lolupena varānane //
2.24.d:
अमतेन पुराणानां व्याहृतं यद्द्विजन्मना ।
क्षुद्रशास्त्रोपदेशेन लोलुपेन वरानने ॥
2.24.m: that which was uttered by that twice-born man, contrary to the mind of the Purāṇas, / taught from inferior treatises because he was greedy, O fair-faced woman:

2.24.s:
purāṇe nirṇayo hyeṣa vidvadbhiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ /
na śaṅkhena pibettoyaṃ na hanyātkūrmasūkarau //
2.24.d:
पुराणे निर्णयो ह्येष विद्वद्भिः समुदाहृतः ।
न शङ्खेन पिबेत्तोयं न हन्यात्कूर्मसूकरौ ॥
2.24.m: this decision in the Purāṇas has indeed been declared by the wise: / one should not drink water from a conch shell; one should not kill a tortoise or a boar;

2.24.s:
ekādaśyāṃ na bhoktavyaṃ pakṣayorubhayorapi /
agamyāgamane devi abhakṣyasya ca bhakṣaṇe //
2.24.d:
एकादश्यां न भोक्तव्यं पक्षयोरुभयोरपि ।
अगम्यागमने देवि अभक्ष्यस्य च भक्षणे ॥
2.24.m: one must not eat on Ekādaśī in both lunar fortnights. / In approaching an unapproachable woman, O goddess, and in eating forbidden food,

2.24.s:
akāryakaraṇe jantorgosahasravadhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
jānannapi kathaṃ devi bhokṣye 'haṃ harivāsare //
2.24.d:
अकार्यकरणे जन्तोर्गोसहस्रवधः स्मृतः ।
जानन्नपि कथं देवि भोक्ष्ये ऽहं हरिवासरे ॥
2.24.m: and in committing forbidden deeds, the sin of a living being is recorded as equal to the slaughter of a thousand cows. / Even knowing this, O goddess, how could I eat on Hari’s day?

2.24.s:
puroḍāśo 'pi vāmoru saṃprāpte harivāsare /
abhakṣyeṇa samaḥ proktaḥ kiṃ punaścāttanakriyā //
2.24.d:
पुरोडाशो ऽपि वामोरु संप्राप्ते हरिवासरे ।
अभक्ष्येण समः प्रोक्तः किं पुनश्चात्तनक्रिया ॥
2.24.m: Even the sacrificial cake, O woman of lovely thighs, when Hari’s day has arrived, / is declared to be equal to uneatable food; how much more so ordinary food?

2.24.s:
anukūlaṃ nṛṇāṃ proktaṃ kṣīṇānāṃ varavarṇini /
mūlaṃ phalaṃ payastoyamupabhojyaṃ munīśvaraiḥ //
2.24.d:
अनुकूलं नृणां प्रोक्तं क्षीणानां वरवर्णिनि ।
मूलं फलं पयस्तोयमुपभोज्यं मुनीश्वरैः ॥
2.24.m: Substitutes have been declared by the best of sages for people who are weak, O fair-complexioned woman: / roots, fruits, milk, and water may be consumed.

2.24.s:
natvatra bhojanaṃ kaiścidekādaśyāṃ pradarśitam /
jvariṇāṃ laṅghanaṃ śastaṃ dhārmikāṇāmupoṣaṇam //
2.24.d:
नत्वत्र भोजनं कैश्चिदेकादश्यां प्रदर्शितम् ।
ज्वरिणां लङ्घनं शस्तं धार्मिकाणामुपोषणम् ॥
2.24.m: However, eating has not been prescribed by any on Ekādaśī. / Fasting is commended for the feverish, and fasting for the righteous.

2.24.s:
śubhaṃ gatipradaṃ proktaṃ saṃprāpte harivāsare /
jvaramadhye kṛtaṃ pathyaṃ nidhanāya prakalpate //
2.24.d:
शुभं गतिप्रदं प्रोक्तं संप्राप्ते हरिवासरे ।
ज्वरमध्ये कृतं पथ्यं निधनाय प्रकल्पते ॥
2.24.m: It is declared auspicious and granting the [highest] state when the day of Hari has arrived; / taking wholesome food in the midst of a fever brings about death.

2.24.s:
vaiṣṇave tu dine bhuktaṃ narakāyaiva kevalam /
māgrahaṃ kuru vāmoru vratabhaṅgo bhavenmama //
2.24.d:
वैष्णवे तु दिने भुक्तं नरकायैव केवलम् ।
माग्रहं कुरु वामोरु व्रतभङ्गो भवेन्मम ॥
2.24.m: Eating on the day of Viṣṇu leads solely to hell. / Do not insist, O fair-thighed one! My vow would be broken.

2.24.s:
yadanyadvocate tubhyaṃ tatkartāsmi na saṃśayaḥ /
mohinyuvāca
na cānyadrocate rājanvinā vai bhojanaṃ tava //
2.24.d:
यदन्यद्वोचते तुभ्यं तत्कर्तास्मि न संशयः ।
मोहिन्युवाच
न चान्यद्रोचते राजन्विना वै भोजनं तव ॥
2.24.m: Whatever else is pleasing to you, that I will do without doubt. / Mohinī said: / Nothing else pleases me, O king, except your eating.

2.24.s:
jīvitasyāpi dānena na me kiñcitprayodajanam /
na ca vedeṣu dṛṣṭo 'yamupavāso harerdine //
2.24.d:
जीवितस्यापि दानेन न मे किञ्चित्प्रयोदजनम् ।
न च वेदेषु दृष्टो ऽयमुपवासो हरेर्दिने ॥
2.24.m: Even by the giving of your life, I have no purpose at all. / Nor is this fasting seen in the Vedas on the day of Hari.

2.24.s:
agnimanto na viprā hi manyante samupoṣaṇam /
vedabāhya kathaṃ dharmaṃ bhavāṃścaritumicchati //
2.24.d:
अग्निमन्तो न विप्रा हि मन्यन्ते समुपोषणम् ।
वेदबाह्य कथं धर्मं भवांश्चरितुमिच्छति ॥
2.24.m: Indeed, the brahmins who keep the sacred fire do not approve of complete fasting. / Why do you wish to practice a duty that is outside the Veda?

2.24.s:
vaco niśamya mohinyā rājā vedavidāṃ varaḥ /
uvāca mānase kruddhaḥ prahasanniva bhūpate //
2.24.d:
वचो निशम्य मोहिन्या राजा वेदविदां वरः ।
उवाच मानसे क्रुद्धः प्रहसन्निव भूपते ॥
2.24.m: Hearing the words of Mohinī, the king, foremost among knowers of the Veda, / was angry in his mind, and, as if laughing, said, O lord of the earth:

2.24.s:
śṛṇu mohini madvākyaṃ vedo 'yaṃ bahudhā sthitaḥ /
yajñakarmakriyā vedaḥ smṛtirvedo gṛhāśrame //
2.24.d:
शृणु मोहिनि मद्वाक्यं वेदो ऽयं बहुधा स्थितः ।
यज्ञकर्मक्रिया वेदः स्मृतिर्वेदो गृहाश्रमे ॥
2.24.m: Listen to my words, O Mohinī: this Veda is established manifoldly. / The Veda is the performance of sacrificial rites; the Veda is the Smṛti in the householder's stage of life;

2.24.s:
smṛtirvedaḥ kriyāvedaḥ purāṇeṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
purāṇapuṃruṣājjātaṃ yathedaṃ jagadadbhutam //
2.24.d:
स्मृतिर्वेदः क्रियावेदः पुराणेषु प्रतिष्ठितः ।
पुराणपुंरुषाज्जातं यथेदं जगदद्भुतम् ॥
2.24.m: The Smṛti-Veda and the Kriyā-Veda are established in the Purāṇas. / Just as this wondrous universe was born from the ancient Puruṣa,

2.24.s:
tathedaṃ vāṅmayaṃ jātaṃ purāṇebhyo na saṃśayaḥ /
vedārthādadhikaṃ manye purāṇārthaṃ varānane //
2.24.d:
तथेदं वाङ्मयं जातं पुराणेभ्यो न संशयः ।
वेदार्थादधिकं मन्ये पुराणार्थं वरानने ॥
2.24.m: so too this entire body of speech was born from the Purāṇas, without doubt. / I consider the meaning of the Purāṇas greater than the meaning of the Vedas, O fair-faced woman!

2.24.s:
vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ sarve purāṇeṣveva sarvadā /
bibhetyalpaśrutādvedo māmayaṃ prahariṣyati //
2.24.d:
वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः सर्वे पुराणेष्वेव सर्वदा ।
बिभेत्यल्पश्रुताद्वेदो मामयं प्रहरिष्यति ॥
2.24.m: All the Vedas are ever established only in the Purāṇas. / The Veda fears one of little learning, thinking: 'He will strike me down!'

2.24.s:
na vede grahasaṃcāro na śuddhiḥ kālabodhinī /
tithivṛddhikṣayo vāpi parvagrahavinirṇayaḥ //
2.24.d:
न वेदे ग्रहसंचारो न शुद्धिः कालबोधिनी ।
तिथिवृद्धिक्षयो वापि पर्वग्रहविनिर्णयः ॥
2.24.m: In the Veda there is no movement of the planets, no purification that instructs concerning time, / nor the increase and decrease of lunar days, nor the determination of eclipse-conjunctions.

2.24.s:
iti hāsapurāṇaistu niścayo 'yaṃ kṛtaḥ purā /
yanna dṛṣṭaṃ hi vedeṣu tatsarvaṃ lakṣyate smṛtau //
2.24.d:
इति हासपुराणैस्तु निश्चयो ऽयं कृतः पुरा ।
यन्न दृष्टं हि वेदेषु तत्सर्वं लक्ष्यते स्मृतौ ॥
2.24.m: This determination was made long ago by the Itihāsas and Purāṇas. / For whatever is not seen in the Vedas is all observed in the Smṛti;

2.24.s:
ubhayoryanna dṛṣṭaṃ hi tatpurāṇaiḥ pragīyate /
prāyaścittaṃ tu hatyāyāmāturasyauṣadhaṃ priye //
2.24.d:
उभयोर्यन्न दृष्टं हि तत्पुराणैः प्रगीयते ।
प्रायश्चित्तं तु हत्यायामातुरस्यौषधं प्रिये ॥
2.24.m: what is not seen in both is proclaimed by the Purāṇas. / Expiation is prescribed for murder, and medicine for the sick, O dear one;

2.24.s:
na cāpi pāpaśuddhiḥ syādātmanaśca parasya vā /
yadvedairgīyate subhru upāṅgairyatpragīyate //
2.24.d:
न चापि पापशुद्धिः स्यादात्मनश्च परस्य वा ।
यद्वेदैर्गीयते सुभ्रु उपाङ्गैर्यत्प्रगीयते ॥
2.24.m: nor could there be purification from sin for oneself or another [without them]. / What is sung by the Vedas, O fair-browed one, what is proclaimed by the secondary limbs,

2.24.s:
purāṇaiḥ smṛtibhiścaiva veda eva nigadyate /
raṭantīha purāṇāni bhūyo bhūyo varānane //
2.24.d:
पुराणैः स्मृतिभिश्चैव वेद एव निगद्यते ।
रटन्तीह पुराणानि भूयो भूयो वरानने ॥
2.24.m: and by the Purāṇas and Smṛtis, is declared to be the Veda itself. / Here the Purāṇas shout repeatedly, O fair-faced woman:

2.24.s:
na bhoktavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ saṃprāpte harivāsare /
purāṇamanyathā matvā tiryagyonimavāpnuyāt //
2.24.d:
न भोक्तव्यं न भोक्तव्यं संप्राप्ते हरिवासरे ।
पुराणमन्यथा मत्वा तिर्यग्योनिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.24.m: 'One must not eat, one must not eat, when the day of Hari has arrived!' / Considering the Purāṇa otherwise, one would obtain rebirth as an animal.

2.24.s:
saṃsrāto 'pi sudānto 'pi na gatiṃ prāpnuyāditi /
pitaraṃ ko na vandeta mātaraṃ ko na pūjayet //
2.24.d:
संस्रातो ऽपि सुदान्तो ऽपि न गतिं प्राप्नुयादिति ।
पितरं को न वन्देत मातरं को न पूजयेत् ॥
2.24.m: Even if well-bathed and well-restrained, he would not attain the [good] state. / Who would not bow to a father? Who would not honor a mother?

2.24.s:
ko na gacchetsaricchreṣṭhāṃ ko bhuṅkte harivāsare /
ko hi dūṣayate vedaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ ko nipātayet //
2.24.d:
को न गच्छेत्सरिच्छ्रेष्ठां को भुङ्क्ते हरिवासरे ।
को हि दूषयते वेदं ब्राह्मणं को निपातयेत् ॥
2.24.m: Who would not go to the best of rivers? Who eats on the day of Hari? / Who indeed vilifies the Veda? Who would bring down a brahmin?

2.24.s: ko gacchetparadārān hi ko bhuṅkte harivāsare //
2.24.d: को गच्छेत्परदारान् हि को भुङ्क्ते हरिवासरे ॥
2.24.m: Who indeed would go to another's wife? Who eats on the day of Hari?

2.24.s:
nahīdṛśaṃ pāpamihāsti jantorvimūḍhacittasya dine hareḥ priye /
yadbhojanenātmanipātakāriṇā yamasya ravāteṣu ciraṃ sulocane //
2.24.d:
नहीदृशं पापमिहास्ति जन्तोर्विमूढचित्तस्य दिने हरेः प्रिये ।
यद्भोजनेनात्मनिपातकारिणा यमस्य रवातेषु चिरं सुलोचने ॥
2.24.m: For there is no such sin in this world, O dear one, for a deluded person on the day of Hari, / as that committed by eating, bringing sin upon oneself [and dwelling] long in the hellish torments of Yama, O woman of beautiful eyes!

2.24.s:
mohinyuvāca
śīghramānaya viprāṃstvaṃ ghūrṇike vedapāragān /
yeṣāṃ vākyena yukto 'yaṃ rājā kuryāddhi bhojanam //
2.24.d:
मोहिन्युवाच
शीघ्रमानय विप्रांस्त्वं घूर्णिके वेदपारगान् ।
येषां वाक्येन युक्तो ऽयं राजा कुर्याद्धि भोजनम् ॥
2.24.m: Mohinī said: / Quickly bring, O Ghūrṇikā, brahmins who have mastered the Vedas, / persuaded by whose words this king may indeed take food.

2.24.s:
sā tadvākyamupākarṇya brāhmaṇānvedaśālinaḥ /
gautamādīnsamāhūya mohinīpārśvamānayata //
2.24.d:
सा तद्वाक्यमुपाकर्ण्य ब्राह्मणान्वेदशालिनः ।
गौतमादीन्समाहूय मोहिनीपार्श्वमानयत ॥
2.24.m: Hearing her words, she summoned the brahmins endowed with Vedic learning, / Gautama and others, and brought them to Mohinī's side.

2.24.s:
tānviprānāgatāndṛṣṭvā vedavedāṅgapāragān /
mohinī sahitā rājñā vavande kāryatatparā //
2.24.d:
तान्विप्रानागतान्दृष्ट्वा वेदवेदाङ्गपारगान् ।
मोहिनी सहिता राज्ञा ववन्दे कार्यतत्परा ॥
2.24.m: Seeing those brahmins arrived, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / Mohinī, intent on her purpose, bowed down along with the king.

2.24.s:
upaviṣṭāstu te sarve śātakaiṃbhamayeṣu ca /
āsaneṣu mahīpāla jvaladagnisamaprabhāḥ //
2.24.d:
उपविष्टास्तु ते सर्वे शातकैंभमयेषु च ।
आसनेषु महीपाल ज्वलदग्निसमप्रभाः ॥
2.24.m: They all sat down on golden seats, / O protector of the earth, possessing a brilliance equal to blazing fire.

2.24.s:
teṣāṃ madhye vayovṛddho gautamo vākyamabravīt /
vayaṃ samāgatā devi nānāśāstraviśāradāḥ //
2.24.d:
तेषां मध्ये वयोवृद्धो गौतमो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
वयं समागता देवि नानाशास्त्रविशारदाः ॥
2.24.m: Among them, Gautama, advanced in age, spoke these words: / 'We have arrived, O queen, skilled in various treatises,

2.24.s:
sarvasaṃdehahartāro yadarthaṃ te samāhutāḥ /
tacchatvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ mohinī brahmaṇaḥ sutā //
2.24.d:
सर्वसंदेहहर्तारो यदर्थं ते समाहुताः ।
तच्छत्वा वचनं तेषां मोहिनी ब्रह्मणः सुता ॥
2.24.m: dispelling all doubts, for which purpose we were summoned.' / Hearing those words of theirs, Mohinī, the daughter of Brahmā,

2.24.s:
sarvāsādhyakṛtaṃ kartuṃ pravṛttāṃstānuvāca ha /
mohinyuvāca
saṃdehastu jaḍau hyeṣa svalpo vā svamatiryathā //
2.24.d:
सर्वासाध्यकृतं कर्तुं प्रवृत्तांस्तानुवाच ह ।
मोहिन्युवाच
संदेहस्तु जडौ ह्येष स्वल्पो वा स्वमतिर्यथा ॥
2.24.m: spoke to those who were ready to accomplish what was impossible to accomplish: / Mohinī said: / 'This doubt is dull indeed, whether small or according to one's own opinion.

2.24.s:
so 'yaṃ vadati rājā vai nāhaṃ bhokṣye harerdine /
annādhāramidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam //
2.24.d:
सो ऽयं वदति राजा वै नाहं भोक्ष्ये हरेर्दिने ।
अन्नाधारमिदं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
2.24.m: Thus this king says: 'I will certainly not eat on Hari’s day. / All this universe, motionless and moving, has food as its support.'

2.24.s:
mṛtā hyapi tathānnena prīyante pitaro divi /
karkandhumātraṃ prahutaṃ puroḍāśaṃ hi devatāḥ //
2.24.d:
मृता ह्यपि तथान्नेन प्रीयन्ते पितरो दिवि ।
कर्कन्धुमात्रं प्रहुतं पुरोडाशं हि देवताः ॥
2.24.m: Even the dead ancestors in heaven are pleased by food. / The deities desire even a sacrificial cake the size of a jujube offered in the fire, O best of the twice-born;

2.24.s:
kāmayanti dvijaśreṣṭhāstato 'nnaṃ hyamṛtaṃ param /
pipīlikāpi kṣudhitā mukhenādāya taṇḍulam //
2.24.d:
कामयन्ति द्विजश्रेष्ठास्ततो ऽन्नं ह्यमृतं परम् ।
पिपीलिकापि क्षुधिता मुखेनादाय तण्डुलम् ॥
2.24.m: therefore food is the supreme nectar. / Even an ant, when hungry, takes a grain of rice in its mouth

2.24.s:
bilaṃ vrajati duḥkhena kasyānnaṃ nahi rocate /
ayaṃ khādati nānnādyaṃ saṃprāpte harivāsare //
2.24.d:
बिलं व्रजति दुःखेन कस्यान्नं नहि रोचते ।
अयं खादति नान्नाद्यं संप्राप्ते हरिवासरे ॥
2.24.m: and enters its hole with difficulty; to whom is food not pleasing? / This [king] does not eat food today when the day of Hari has arrived.

2.24.s:
nijadharmaṃ parityajya paradharme vyavasthitaḥ /
vidhāvānāṃ yatīnāṃ ca yujyate vratasevanam //
2.24.d:
निजधर्मं परित्यज्य परधर्मे व्यवस्थितः ।
विधावानां यतीनां च युज्यते व्रतसेवनम् ॥
2.24.m: Abandoning his own duty, he is established in the duty of another. / The observance of vows is suitable for widows and ascetics.

2.24.s:
paradharmarato yaḥ syātsvadharmavimukho naraḥ /
soṃ'dhe tamasi majjeta yāvadindrāścaturddaśa //
2.24.d:
परधर्मरतो यः स्यात्स्वधर्मविमुखो नरः ।
सोंऽधे तमसि मज्जेत यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्द्दश ॥
2.24.m: A man who is devoted to the duty of another and averse to his own duty / would sink into blind darkness for as long as fourteen Indras [rule].

2.24.s:
upavāsādikaraṇaṃ bhūbhujāṃ noditaṃ kvacit /
prajāsaṃrakṣaṇaṃ tyaktvā caturvargaphalapradam //
2.24.d:
उपवासादिकरणं भूभुजां नोदितं क्वचित् ।
प्रजासंरक्षणं त्यक्त्वा चतुर्वर्गफलप्रदम् ॥
2.24.m: The performance of fasts and the like has nowhere been prescribed for kings, / setting aside the protection of the subjects, which yields the fruit of the four aims of life.

2.24.s:
nārīṇāṃ bhartṛśūśrūṣā putrāṇāṃ pitṛsevanam /
śūdrāṇāṃ dvijasevā ca lokarakṣā mahībhṛtām //
2.24.d:
नारीणां भर्तृशूश्रूषा पुत्राणां पितृसेवनम् ।
शूद्राणां द्विजसेवा च लोकरक्षा महीभृताम् ॥
2.24.m: The duty of women is service to the husband; of sons, service to the father; / of Śūdras, service to the twice-born; and of kings, protection of the world.

2.24.s:
svakaṃ karma parityajya yo 'nyatra kurute śramam /
ajñānādvā pramādācca patitaḥ sa na saṃśayaḥ //
2.24.d:
स्वकं कर्म परित्यज्य यो ऽन्यत्र कुरुते श्रमम् ।
अज्ञानाद्वा प्रमादाच्च पतितः स न संशयः ॥
2.24.m: He who abandons his own duty and exerts himself in another's, / whether out of ignorance or negligence, is fallen; of this there is no doubt.

2.24.s:
so 'yamadya mahīpālo yatidharmme vyavasthitaḥ /
subuddhyācāraśīlaśca vedoktaṃ tyajati dvijāḥ //
2.24.d:
सो ऽयमद्य महीपालो यतिधर्म्मे व्यवस्थितः ।
सुबुद्ध्याचारशीलश्च वेदोक्तं त्यजति द्विजाः ॥
2.24.m: This ruler of the earth is today established in the duty of an ascetic; / though having a disposition toward good intellect and conduct, he abandons what is spoken in the Veda, O twice-born!

2.24.s:
svecchācārā tu yā nārī yo 'vinītaḥ suto dvijāḥ /
ekāntaśīlo nṛpatirbhṛtyaḥ karmavivarjitaḥ //
2.24.d:
स्वेच्छाचारा तु या नारी यो ऽविनीतः सुतो द्विजाः ।
एकान्तशीलो नृपतिर्भृत्यः कर्मविवर्जितः ॥
2.24.m: A woman who acts according to her own will, an undisciplined son, O twice-born, / a king who loves solitude, and a servant devoid of work—

2.24.s:
sarve te narakaṃ yānti hyapratiṣṭhaśca yo dvijāḥ /
ayaṃ hi niyamopeto haripūjanatatparaḥ //
2.24.d:
सर्वे ते नरकं यान्ति ह्यप्रतिष्ठश्च यो द्विजाः ।
अयं हि नियमोपेतो हरिपूजनतत्परः ॥
